Whether it be a man or a woman, both endowed with all enjoyments, shall dwell in the world of Durgā for a kalpa and then return here once again.
Endowed with wealth and grain, they are born into the families of great men; they are fortunate and handsome, proud of their beauty and youth. || 38 ||
O Goddess, having attained this human state—which is difficult to find and as flickering as a flash of lightning—may these two become vessels of all happiness. (39)
For him by whom that Lalitā has been seen, whence can there be fear of rebirth?
Whatever fruit a man obtains by performing a circumambulation of the earth [is attained by him]. || 40 ||
That fruit [is obtained] from the manifestation of Lalitā in Vārāṇasī;
indeed, by fasting at that time on the fourth lunar day month after month. || 41 ||
Having worshipped that goddess, one should observe a vigil there;
O Goddess, her prosperity shall be complete, for she is honored even by the three worlds. 42.
O Mohinī, by worshipping that [deity] Nalakūbara Keśava, who bestows all spiritual perfections, a person becomes one who has accomplished all his purposes. || 43 ||
O Goddess, to the south of that very place is the one known as Maṇikarṇikā;
and in front of it is a great holy site (tīrtha) that destroys all sins.
Having seen, bowed to, and duly worshipped the Lord Maṇikarṇīśvara situated within the sacrificial pit, one shall not dwell in a womb again.
On its southern bank, on the Gaṅgā, is situated the supreme Gaṅgeśvara; by worshipping him, one shall attain the world of the gods. || 46 ||
O highly deluded one, I shall describe another sacred site in Vārāṇasī, where there is indeed the beautiful and desired abode of the God of gods. || 47 ||
O blessed lady, in former times, the linga of the moon-crested Lord was being swiftly carried away through the sky by Rākṣasas moving in the firmament. || 48 ||
When he arrived in this place, the Lord thought:
"How may I never again be separated from Avimukta? (49)
O auspicious one, while the Lord of Gods was reflecting upon this matter,
the sound of a cock suddenly arose in that place.
O Goddess, having heard that sound, the Rākṣasas, their minds filled with terror,
abandoned the linga right there and departed at the time of dawn.
When the Rākṣasas had thus departed, the Lord himself, the God of gods, remained present right there at that exceedingly beautiful and auspicious spot as a sacred emblem (liṅga).
In the midst of that Avimukta, it is known as even more liberated (Avimuktatara). || 53 ||

Then, as the gods remembered the name of Hara—which is rich with most meritorious syllables and bestows liberation upon all beings, both stationary and moving—those living creatures who were passing away there [were liberated]. (54)
O fortunate one, cocks also always remain in that place;
even today they are seen there, being worshipped by those of auspicious nature. || 55 ||
O Goddess, for that man who takes refuge in Avimukta with the vision of initiation,
there is no return to rebirth even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
To the south of the God stands a beautiful pond;
by drinking its water, one shall not return here again. 57.
Three signs appear in the heart of a man;
those men by whom that water was thus drunk have indeed accomplished their purpose.
There is no doubt that they indeed possess the liberating knowledge, having bathed in the waters of the pond and beheld the one named Daṇḍaka. (59)
Having seen Avimukta from there, one attains liberation in an instant;
by performing the twilight worship there even once, a Brāhmaṇa [achieves this]. 60.
For sixty-five years, he would have performed his devotions at that city of Vārāṇasī and at the Avimukta cremation ground.
And by beholding Avimukteśvara, one becomes a leader of the Gaṇas;
indeed, by merely seeing the Avimukteśvara Liṅga there, a human being [attains this state]. || 62 ||
One is immediately liberated from sins, as well as from diseases and the bonds of worldly existence;
moreover, at the front of Avimukta stands a linga facing westward.
And that [place], O blessed lady, is indeed named Avimukta and Lakṣaṇeśvara;
by merely seeing it, a man becomes possessed of knowledge.
And to the north of that, O Goddess, is the four-faced Liṅga known as Caturtheśvara; it is supreme for liberating one from fear of sin.
The sacred field named Vārāṇasī bestows liberation upon living beings on earth;
there, Avimukteśvara is celebrated as one who is liberated while still alive.
For one situated anywhere at all, the status of a Gaṇapati is ordained;
moreover, by relinquishing one's vital breaths there, one shall attain ultimate liberation.
Within this field, the first enclosure is thus remembered;
likewise, in the second enclosure, Maṇikarṇikā is situated in the east.
Indeed, seventy million lingas are situated in that place;
by the mere sight of them, one obtains the fruit of sacrifices. || 69 ||
These are the established liṅgas; likewise, the wells, the meritorious lakes, the ponds, the rivers, and the springs are also proclaimed as such. || 70 ||
And whoever, with a concentrated mind, shall perform an ablution in these very [waters] and touch the lingas, shall not enter into saṃsāra again. (71)
Whatever sacred fords (tīrthas) exist upon the earth and those which are in the intermediate space—
among them, I have indeed proclaimed to you the principal ones.
O lady of beautiful hips, this pilgrimage to sacred fords has been described as the destroyer of sins;
whoever performs it or even witnesses it shall indeed become a partaker of liberation. (73)
But Avimukta, O fair-hipped one, is the beautiful middle enclosure;
it is indeed named Kaṇṭaka, which bestows immortality at the time of death. (74)

Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Pilgrimage," in the *Kāśīmāhātmya* section of the dialogue between Vasu and Mohinī within the latter part of the glorious *Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa*.
Thus ends the fifty-first chapter.
Vasu said:
O Mohinī, hereafter I shall describe the proper time for the pilgrimage.
But that which was performed by the gods today bestows fruits according to what is appropriate.
In ancient times, this festival was established by the gods in the month of Caitra, while they remained there at Kāmakuṇḍa, intent upon bathing and worship.
O lady of auspicious countenance, in the month of Jyeṣṭha, the Siddhas indeed performed a pilgrimage at the Rudravāsa Kuṇḍa, being devoted to bathing and worship.
Moreover, in the month of Āṣāḍha, this pilgrimage was established by the auspicious Gandharvas at the pool of Priyādevī, through those who perform ablutions and worship.
This pilgrimage was performed by the Vidyādharas in the month of Śrāvaṇa at Mohinī, while they were devoted to bathing and worship at Lakṣmīkuṇḍa. || 5 ||
O fair-faced one, this was performed by the Yakṣas residing at the Mārkaṇḍeya lake, who were intent on bathing and worship, during the month of Vaiśākha.
And in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, O Mohinī, this pilgrimage was performed by crores of serpents stationed at Koṭitīrtha, who engaged in the rites of bathing and worship.
O lady of auspicious eyes, in the month of Pauṣa, a pilgrimage was undertaken by the Guhyakas residing at Kapālamocana, accompanied by ritual bathing, meditation, and worship.
In the auspicious month of Phālguna, a pilgrimage was performed by Piśācas residing in the pool known as Kāleśvara, who were intent upon bathing, worship, and other rites.
In the auspicious month of Phālguna, on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, O Goddess, it is therefore proclaimed as the one renowned by the name Piśācī.
Now, O fair-faced one, I shall fully explain to you the ritual for the journey, by performing which a person obtains the fruit of the journey. (11)
Water-pots, however, should be given along with sweet food, provided with fruits and flowers, auspicious and covered with cloths. || 12 ||
On the third day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, which yields great fruit, Gaurī should be beheld by men with a spirit of devotion. || 13 ||
Having performed your bath, O lady of beautiful countenance, you should proceed to Goprekṣa;
there, at Svardvāra, the goddess Kālikā must be worshipped with great effort.
Another supreme [form] has also been proclaimed, the auspicious Saṃvartalalitā;
she should indeed be beheld with devotion, for she bestows the fruits of all desires. || 15 ||
Then, one should feed the Brahmins who are devotees of Śiva and observant of pure vows, with garments and abundant sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) according to their merit.
Having dedicated them to the five Gaurīs, one should offer juices and perfumes to a brāhmaṇa;
thus, endowed with good fortune, one attains the highest welfare. || 17 ||
O Goddess, I shall now describe the Vināyakas who cause obstacles within the dwelling of a sacred field; by worshipping them, a person obtains the fruit [of their efforts] without hindrance. (18)
Having first seen Ḍhuṇḍhi, as well as Kilavināyaka, the Vināyaka of the Goddess, Goprekṣa, and Hastihastin; || 19 ||
Likewise, another Vināyaka, renowned by the name Sindūrya, should be seen on the fourth day, O Goddess; thus indeed are the Vināyakas to be beheld.
And sweetmeat balls (laḍḍukas) should be offered dedicated to these Brahmins;
by this very rite, a man becomes successful. || 21 ||
Hereafter, I shall describe the Caṇḍikās who protect the sacred field: Durgā protects in the south, and Antareśvarī in the southwest. || 22 ||
Aṅgāreśī is in the west, Bhadrakālikā in the northwest,
Bhīmacaṇḍā in the north, and likewise Mahāmattā in the northeast.
Ūrddhvakeśī joined with Samāyuktā is remembered as being in the east; Śāṅkarī is in the southeast, while Adhaḥkeśī and Citraghaṇṭā are in the center.
Whosoever among men beholds these goddesses Caṇḍikās, they all, being pleased, protect that sacred field with devoted intent. || 25 ||
O Goddess, they constantly create obstacles for sinners at all times;
therefore, the goddesses, together with Vināyaka, should always be worshipped for the sake of protection. || 26 ||
If one desires supreme accomplishment, progeny, prosperity, and happiness, then one should offer perfumes, flowers, food offerings, and so forth with devotion. || 27 ||
Moreover, O fair-eyed one, I shall tell you another thing regarding that place: three rivers with auspicious waters flow there.
By the mere sight of them, the sin of killing a Brahmin is removed;
among them, one is the Trisrotas and another is the Mandākinī.
Matsyodarī is the third; these three are givers of merit.
There, the holy Mandākinī is situated at Madhyameśvara.
The Trisrotikā is established there, as well as the Avimuktā which bestows merit;
however, the Matsyodarī at Oṃkāra always indeed bestows merit.
When the enchanting Gaṅgā arrives at that place, it will then be a most meritorious time, difficult to attain even for the gods. || 32 ||
Having bathed there in that holy lord of rivers, whose waters are sprinkled by the Varaṇā and flooded by the waters of the Jāhnavī, why should one grieve?
O auspicious one, when the Gaṅgā became united with the Matsyodarī, at that time Śiva was freed from his skull through bathing.
In that very place is a very great lake named Kapālamocana, which is proclaimed to be purifying for all beings and bestowing merit. || 35 ||
Then, having bathed in the waters of Matsyodarī near Oṃkāreśvara and having beheld the Lord Oṃkāra in those waters, [he attained liberation].
A person who has bathed there is not touched by sorrow, old age, death, or bondage; he becomes Śiva himself, known by the name Oṃkāreśvara. || 37 ||
O fair-faced one, out of affection for you, this laughter has been explained; it is proclaimed as consisting of the syllable 'a', the syllable 'u', and the syllable 'm'. (38)
The letter 'A' should be known to be there, bestowing the attainment of the world of Viṣṇu;
on its right side, however, the letter 'U' is proclaimed. || 39 ||
There, having attained supreme perfection, Bṛhaspati, the teacher of the gods,
recognized the syllable Oṃ as the imperishable state of Brahman.
Likewise, on the northern part of those two is the syllable *Makāra*, known as Viṣṇu;
in that liṅga, the great sage Kapila Ṛṣi attained perfection.
Having approached Vārāṇasī, the supreme abode of the five,
Bhīṣma remained there, worshipping the Lord of Gods.
In that auspicious place, Śiva himself appeared, renowned as Goprekṣaka and praised by all the deities. (43)
Having gone to Goprekṣeśvara, seen it, and worshipped it, a person does not meet with misfortune and is liberated from all taints. || 44 ||
Then the cows dwelling in the forest, being scorched by the forest fire, came to this lake while wandering about; once they had reached it, they were cooled and drank the water.
From that time forth, it has been called Kapilāhrada;
and there too, Śiva himself is remembered as Vṛṣadhvaja.
The Lord, being visible, has established his presence here; having bathed in this Kapilāhrada-tīrtha with a restrained mind, he remains forever present.
Upon seeing Śiva, whose banner bears the bull, one obtains the fruit of all sacrifices;
having worshipped him there, one attains the heavenly world after death and becomes Śiva himself. || 48 ||
Upon the dissolution of the body, he attains the state of a Gaṇa, which is exceedingly difficult to obtain;
for in this very place, the cows themselves were indeed created by Brahmā.
For the sake of the peace of all the worlds and to surely purify everyone,
there is the auspicious, meritorious, and sin-removing Bhadradohaka lake.
A man who bathes in that place shall become Vāgīśvara himself; Śiva was brought there and installed by Parameṣṭhin.
Having also taken [the linga] from Brahmā, Viṣṇu established it once again;
Śiva remained there under the name Hiraṇyagarbha. || 52 ||
Furthermore, Brahmā then established a linga known as Svarlokeśvara, which is the divine play (svarlīla) of the Cause (Kāraṇa), somewhere within the heavenly realm.
Having indeed beheld that Lord of Gods, one is glorified in the world of Śiva;
having cast off one's life-breaths here, one is never born again anywhere.
Infinite is that goal which is prescribed for yogis alone;
even in this very land, there was a Daitya who was a thorn in the side of the gods.
Having assumed the form of a tiger, the proud and powerful one was slain;
known as Vyāghreśvara, he remains eternally stationed there.
Furthermore, one does not go to an evil rebirth after beholding this Lord of the Immortals, the Liṅga established on the Himavat mountain, which stands as Śaileśvara. || 57 ||
O auspicious lady, having seen this, a man shall not fall into an evil rebirth— even those two Daityas, Utpala and Vidala, [who were spared] by virtue of Brahmā’s boon.
Seeing that both had been slain by Pārvatī out of her pride regarding her passion for women, he killed the deer here with his arrow; this [mark] remains as his sign.
Having seen this Liṅga situated at Jyeṣṭhasthāna, O blessed lady, a man does not grieve again; he becomes perfected in birth after birth.
Liṅgas were installed all around it by the gods;
and upon seeing them, a mortal indeed becomes a member of the Gaṇas at the dissolution of the body. || 61 ||
And this river Vārāṇasī is meritorious and a destroyer of sins;
having adorned this sacred field, it has joined with the Jāhnavī.
At this confluence, the supreme Liṅga was installed by Brahmā;
let it be seen in the world as renowned as Saṅgameśvara. (63)
For that person who bathes at the auspicious confluence of the two divine rivers and worships Saṅgameśāna, whence can there be any fear of rebirth? (64)
O blessed lady, this Liṅga was installed by Śukra, the son of Bhṛgu; it is named Śukreśvara and is worshipped by all the Siddhas and immortals.
Upon seeing this, a human being is instantly liberated from all sins;
and when that man dies, he does not undergo rebirth in saṃsāra.
O Mohinī, the Daitya Jambuka was slain here by Mahādeva;
having beheld that Liṅga, a person shall obtain all desires. || 67 ||
Know that these meritorious liṅgas, which grant all desires, were indeed established by the gods led by Śakra. || 68 ||
Thus, O Mohinī, all these Śivaliṅgas in this sacred field of Avimuktaka have been described by me to you.
Thus ends the fiftieth chapter, titled "The Greatness of Kāśī," in the dialogue between Mohinī and Vasu within the latter portion of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa. || 50 ||
Now begins the fifty-first chapter.
Vasu said:
Now I shall proclaim to you another supreme majesty of the Gaṅgā.
O auspicious lady, it is situated in Vārāṇasī and bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Whatever is performed at Avimukta attains imperishability;
no sinner who has gone to Avimukta goes to hell.
Whatever sin has been committed against Avimukta becomes like a thunderbolt against that which is auspicious;
and whatever holy places exist throughout the three worlds that grant liberation, [all are surpassed by it]. || 3 ||
They constantly resort to the Ganges as it flows northward in Kāśī;
having bathed at Daśāśvamedha and beheld Śiva, the Lord of the Universe, [one attains liberation].
Becoming instantly free from sin, one is released from the bonds of worldly existence; for the Gaṅgā is meritorious in every respect and is the remover of even the murder of a Brahmin.
Especially in Vārāṇasī, at the confluence of the northward-flowing Varaṇā and this Jāhnavī, a man [attains the supreme goal]. || 6 ||
By merely bathing in the northward-flowing Gaṅgā at Kāśī during the month of Kārtika, one is liberated from all sins.
Having bathed during the month of Māgha, they are liberated from great sins and other heinous crimes, as well as from all those sacred fords (tīrthas) renowned throughout all the worlds.
O fortunate one, all these holy places, together with their sacred shrines, constantly flow toward the Jāhnavī at Kāśī on every auspicious festival day.
Every day the Gaṅgā flows toward the north at Kāśī,
providing for those defiled by the taints of great sins and the like the merit arising from her touch.

And for the sake of removing one's own evil and for the liberation from the sins of all living beings—even for one who is devoted to virtuous deeds throughout hundreds of future births—[this is necessary]. (11)
O auspicious lady, elsewhere a wise person may or may not attain liberation even in a single birth; but here, it is attained by dying in the Gaṅgā.
Liberation is attained at Kāśī by a man whose mind is free from attachment;
O beautiful one, right there is the famous lake known as Dharmanada.
Dharma itself, by its very nature, is the destroyer of great sins;
and that auspicious Dhūtapāpā is composed of all sacred fords (tīrthas). 14.
The rays of the Sun destroy the multitude of great sins like trees growing on a riverbank, and the Sarasvatī, with her holy waters, purifies one from sin.
The Gaṅgā and the Yamunā—these five rivers are proclaimed;
therefore, this sacred site (tīrtha) is renowned throughout the three worlds by the name Pañcanada.
One who has not bathed there should not assume a physical body composed of the five elements at this confluence of the five rivers, which shatters the flood of sins.
Merely by bathing at Prayāga during the month of Māgha, a man attains that fruit which results from a perfect bath after having pierced through the pavilion of the universe.
That fruit shall certainly be attained in a single day at Pañcanada in Kāśī by bathing in the Pañcanada Tīrtha and performing the libations for the ancestors. (19)
By worshipping Viṣṇu Mādhava, one shall not undergo birth again;
for as many sesame seeds as are offered to the ancestors in the water-libation, [so many years shall they dwell in heaven].
For those who have performed a śrāddha with faith at the auspicious holy site of Pañcanada, there shall be satisfaction lasting for a year in the meritorious tīrtha of Pañcanada.
Even though their grandfathers were liberated while in various states of existence, this verse is sung by the hosts of ancestors in the world of Yama: || 22 ||
"Having seen the greatness of the Pañcanada [region], someone born in our lineage will also perform a śrāddha here according to the prescribed rites. (23)
Having reached Pañcanada in Kāśī, by which we may be liberated—whatever wealth is given there at that sacred ford (tīrtha) of Pañcanada [is of great merit]. || 24 ||
Even at the end of an aeon, there shall be no exhaustion of that merit for one who, though barren, bathes for a year in the Pañcanada pool.
Having worshipped Maṅgalā-Gaurī with waters from the Pañcanada region, purified by a cloth, one certainly gives birth to a son. || 26 ||
By bathing the one renowned in all directions here with one hundred and eight jars of the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), one obtains a great fruit. || 27 ||
That [water] from the Pañcanada region, when weighed, attained superiority;
indeed, by drinking it five times with a *pañcakūrca* [strainer], purification for the pilgrimage is proclaimed. || 28 ||

That purification comes from drinking a drop of the waters of the five rivers with faith; furthermore, it results from bathing in the lake [of Puṣkara] or from performing the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices. || 29 ||
The fruit of that is said to be increased a hundredfold by the water of the Pañcanada;
furthermore, the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices become means for attaining heaven.
Liberation from the pair of Brahma’s slabs by the waters of the five rivers is esteemed by the virtuous even more than the consecration by the celestial river. (31)
The Pañcanada consecration is peerless and bestows boons;
the fruit that is obtained by performing penance for a hundred years in the Kṛta age is attained here [by this rite]. || 32 ||

That which is obtained through the merit of all desired sacrifices and charitable works performed throughout one's entire life is attained by bathing just once at Pañcanada during the month of Kārtika.
Elsewhere there may be a greater fruit from the waters of the Pañcanada, but there is no sacred site on the surface of the earth equal to Dhūtapāpa. 34.
That sin accumulated over three lifetimes which might perish from a single bath—what was known as Dharmanada in the Kṛta age and Dhūtapātaka in the Tretā age—[is destroyed here]. (35)
In the Dvāpara age it is known as Bindutīrtha, and in the Kali age it is remembered as Pañcanada;
having given even a single kṛṣṇala of gold at Bindutīrtha, a man [attains great merit].
He shall never be poor anywhere, nor shall he ever be separated from happiness; [he shall possess] cattle, land, sesame, gold, horses, garments, food, dwellings, and ornaments. (37)
Whatever one gives here at Bindu-tīrtha, one obtains inexhaustible merit;
even by offering a single oblation into a well-kindled fire according to the prescribed rite. || 38 ||
At the meritorious Dharmanadī-tīrtha, one obtains the fruit of ten million fire-sacrifices (koṭihoma),
yet it cannot equal the infinite majesty of the Pañcanada-tīrtha.
"Who is capable of describing [the full extent of] Kāśī, the auspicious abode of the four aims of life?
Thus, O blessed lady, I have related to you this supreme majesty of Kāśī. (40)
It bestows happiness and liberation upon men, and destroys even great sins; it redeems the slayer of a Brahmin, the drinker of intoxicants, the thief of gold, and the violator of the guru’s bed. (41)
Even one joined with great sins (mahāpātaka) or even joined with minor sins (upapātaka) shall attain purification by hearing the majesty of Avimukta. || 42 ||
A Brāhmaṇa shall be a knower of the Vedas; a Kṣatriya, victorious in battle; a Vaiśya, a lord of wealth; and a Śūdra, one who associates with devotees of Viṣṇu. (43)
O fortunate one, by hearing this or even by reciting it, may there arise that merit which comes from all sacrifices and that fruit which comes from all sacred fords. (44)
One obtains all that through reading or even hearing it;
a seeker of knowledge gains knowledge, and a seeker of wealth gains wealth. (45)
One seeking a wife shall obtain a wife; one seeking a son shall obtain a son.
Thus have I proclaimed to you the majesty of Avimukta.
It should be given to one devoted to Viṣṇu, to one who delights in devotion to Śiva, to one devoted to the progenitor of the world, and to one who serves Sūrya and Heramba. (47)
By giving [this] to one who desires to serve the guru, one obtains the fruit of bathing at a sacred pilgrimage site;
but by giving it to a rogue, a slanderer, an enemy of cows, Brahmins, and gods, or to one who harms the guru or is envious, one shall meet with death.
Thus ends the fifty-first chapter, titled "The Greatness of Kāśī," in the dialogue between Vasu and Mohinī within the latter portion of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa. || 51 ||
Now the fifty-second chapter.
Mohinī said:
"O best of brahmins, you are blessed; you are compassionate toward all living beings."
That supreme majesty of Kāśī which you have heard from your lotus-like mouth.
Now I have attained my purpose, for I have been awakened by you, O compassionate one; having fallen, I have been rescued from the ocean of worldly existence. || 2 ||
Now, O giver of honor, I desire to hear the majesty of Hari’s sacred field, by going to which a man becomes one who has fulfilled his purpose.
Indeed, it is heard in the Purāṇas and described by sages and the twice-born that the sacred field (kṣetra) of Viṣṇu, the Supreme Person, bestows liberation. || 4 ||
Therefore, let it be told, O illustrious one, if I am dear to you;
for the virtuous are ever intent on benefiting the entire world. (5)
Vasu said: Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim to you the supreme majesty of the sacred field named Puruṣottama, as declared by Brahmā.
On earth, Bhāratavarṣa is declared to be the land of action;
therein, within Bhāratavarṣa, there dwells one situated on the shore of the southern ocean.
It is proclaimed as Utkalā, the bestower of heaven and liberation;
it extends from the ocean as far as the Viraja-maṇḍala.
That region is adorned with all the virtues of those whose conduct is meritorious; it contains all holy fords and sacred shrines.
O large-eyed one, those [sites] are to be known as being in Utkala, on the northern shore of the ocean, in that most excellent region.
There lies the supreme secret field, which bestows liberation, destroys sin, is everywhere strewn with sand, is pure, and grants both dharma and desire. || 11 ||
A field ten yojanas in extent is extremely difficult to obtain,
just as the moon is among the stars or the ocean is among all bodies of water.
Likewise, Puruṣottama is the most excellent among all holy places (tīrthas), just as Pāvaka is among the Vasus and Śaṅkara is among the Rudras. || 13 ||
For in the same way, Puruṣottama is indeed the most excellent of all sacred fords (tīrthas), just as the Brāhmaṇa is among the social classes (varṇas) and Vainateya is among the birds. || 14 ||
Likewise, Puruṣottama is the most excellent among all holy places (tīrthas), just as Skanda is among army commanders and Kapila is among the perfected ones (siddhas). || 15 ||
He was like Airāvata among the lords of elephants, like Bhṛgu among the great seers, like Meru among the peaked mountains, and like the Himalaya among the Nagas. || 16 ||
As Uccaiḥśravas is among horses, as Uśanas is among poets, as Vyāsa is among sages, and as Kubera is among Yakṣas and Rākṣasas; || 17 ||
Just as the mind is among the senses, as the earth is among the elements, as the aśvattha is among all trees, and as the wind is among purifiers; || 18 ||
Just as Arundhatī is among women, as the thunderbolt is among weapons, as the letter 'A' is among all letters, and as the Gāyatrī is among meters; || 19 ||
Just as the head is considered the best among all limbs, so too is the knowledge of liberation (mokṣavidyā) traditionally held to be supreme among all branches of learning. || 20 ||
As a king is among men, as the wish-fulfilling cow is among cows, as gold is among all minerals, and as Vāsuki is among serpents; || 21 ||
Prahlāda was among all the Daityas as Rāma is among those who wield weapons, as the makara is among the fish, and as the king of beasts is among the deer. || 22 ||
Just as Varuṇa is among the aquatic beings, as Yama is among those who exercise restraint, as the Ocean of Milk is among the oceans, and as Nārada is among the divine sages; || 23 ||
Just as the individual soul is among domestic priests, as Time is among those who reckon, as the Sun is among the planets, and as the Praṇava is among mantras; || 24 ||
Likewise, by seeing Śrī Puruṣottama— known as Puruṣa— once, who performs the duty of dharma for all tasks, one is considered to have seen [the Lord] once within the limits of the ocean.
Having once known the knowledge of Brahman, there is no dwelling in a womb again;
such a field, endowed with all virtues, is exceedingly difficult to attain. (26)
O lady of beautiful hips, there dwells the world-pervading, universal soul, the Lord of Gods, Puruṣottama, who is renowned as Puruṣottama. (27)
The source of the world, the Lord of the world—therein everything is established:
the Unborn, Śakra, Rudra, and the gods led by Agni. (28)
O highly fortunate lady, indeed Gandharvas, Apsarases, Siddhas, Pitṛs, gods, and humans always dwell in that region. || 29 ||
The Yakṣas and Vidyādharas, as well as the sages of celebrated vows, the Ṛṣis such as the Vālakhilyas, and the lords of progeny such as Kaśyapa; || 30 ||
The Suparṇas, Kinnaras, Nāgas, and likewise other inhabitants of heaven, as well as the four Vedas with their auxiliary limbs and various Śāstras. || 31 ||
The Itihāsas and Purāṇas, sacrifices with abundant sacrificial fees, various holy rivers, sacred fords, and shrines; || 32 ||
The oceans and likewise the mountains are situated in that region; thus it is a most meritorious land, frequented by gods, sages, and ancestors.
To whom would dwelling in a place endowed with all enjoyments not be pleasing?
What other excellence could there be for that deity superior to this? (34)
Blessed are those men, renowned like the gods themselves, who dwell in Utkala, where the Lord of the World, Puruṣottama, the bestower of liberation, resides. (35)
Having bathed in the waters of the king of holy fords (Tīrtharāja) and beheld Puruṣottama, those mortals dwell in heaven; they do not, however, reside in the abode of Yama.
The lives of those highly intelligent people of Oḍra who dwell in the holy field of Śrī Puruṣottama, in Utkala, are truly fruitful. (37)
Those who behold him with his slightly copper-hued lips, his clear and long eyes, his beautiful eyebrows, hair, and crown, and his lovely, curved ear-lobes; || 38 ||
He possessed a charming smile and beautiful teeth, was adorned with lovely earrings,
and had a fine nose, beautiful cheeks, a handsome forehead, and auspicious marks.
O Goddess, in former times during the Kṛta Yuga, he who possessed prowess equal to Śakra beheld the lotus-face of Kṛṣṇa, which generates joy for the three worlds. (40)
There was a glorious king known as Indradyumna,
who was truthful, pure, skillful, and the best among all wielders of weapons.
He was handsome, fortunate, heroic, a giver, an enjoyer, sweet-spoken, a performer of all sacrifices, devoted to the Brahmins, and true to his promise. || 42 ||
Skilled and accomplished in the science of archery, in the Vedas, and in the treatises,
he was beloved by men and women like the moon on a full-moon night.
Difficult to behold like the sun, sweet as the moon, truly possessed of the nature of Viṣṇu, he was endowed with truth, having conquered anger and mastered his senses. || 44 ||
Devoted to inner knowledge, eager for battle, and intent upon righteousness—thus may that king, a mine of all virtues, protect the earth. (45)
The thought arose within him regarding the propitiation of Viṣṇu:
"How shall I worship Janārdana, the God of gods? (46)
Then, intent on such thoughts, he surveyed the earth with his mind, [considering] in which field, sacred ford, riverbank, or hermitage [he might dwell].
Having beheld all the holy fords that remove sin,
and having reflected upon them all, he went back again in his mind.
Having gone there with his abundant army and vehicles, the king reached that world-renowned, supreme sacred field of Puruṣottama, which bestows liberation.
Having caused a palace of great height to be built, he who gave profuse sacrificial fees performed the horse sacrifice according to the prescribed rites, bestowing abundant gifts.
There, the valiant lord of the earth, having installed Saṅkarṣaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, and Subhadrā, duly performed the Pañcatīrtha rite.
Having worshipped Puruṣottama daily according to the rules with devotion— performing bathing, giving gifts, recitation of mantras, burnt offerings, and likewise beholding the deity—
he then attained liberation through the grace of the God of gods.
Mohinī said: "In that excellent, meritorious, and Vaiṣṇava field, Puruṣottama," || 53 ||
O Lord, was there formerly an image of Viṣṇu well-established there, because that king went there with his army and vehicles? (54)
He established Kṛṣṇa, Rāma, and Bhadrā, the bestower of auspiciousness;
O best of the twice-born, there is a great doubt and wonder regarding that matter.
"I wish to hear all of that; tell me the reason for it.
Vasu said:
"Listen to this ancient account, a narrative that destroys all sin. (56)
I shall relate in brief that which was asked of me by Śrī in the past, on the golden peak of Mount Sumeru, which is endowed with every marvel.
Having bowed her head to the Lord of the World, the imperishable creator of the world, who was stationed there, the Goddess, desiring the welfare of the worlds, [spoke]. (58)
She asked this great question regarding the unsurpassed station on earth. Śrī said:
"Speak, O Lord of all worlds, [and dispel] the doubt residing in my heart. (59)

In the world of mortals, which is full of great wonders, on this earth where [right] action is so difficult to find, in the great ocean of desire and anger with its massive crocodiles of greed and delusion. || 60 ||
O Lord of the Self, there is no one in this world besides you who can provide the definitive resolution of doubts regarding how one may be liberated from the difficult ocean of saṃsāra. (61)
Having heard these words of hers, Janārdana, the God of gods,
spoke with supreme affection a discourse that was the highest essence, like nectar,
easy to practice, easily accomplished, effortless, and of great fruit.
The Blessed Lord said:
"O Goddess, there exists a preeminent sacred site, renowned as Puruṣottama. (63)
O Goddess of the Gods, there exists nothing equal to it in the three worlds; by chanting it, one is liberated from all sins. 64.
O lady of beautiful countenance, this was not known by all men, nor by the Daityas, nor by the Dānavas; it has been revealed by the foremost sages, such as Marīci and others. 65.
On the shore of the southern ocean stands a banyan tree,
which appeared when the great calamity of the falling meteors occurred at the beginning of the kalpa.
It does not undergo destruction at all, but remains established right there;
for as soon as that banyan tree was seen, he repeatedly took refuge in its shade. (67)
Even the sin of killing a Brahmin is liberated from those beings who have performed circumambulations and prostrations; what need is there to mention other sins? (68)
Having shaken off all their sins, they indeed went to the abode of Keśava,
located slightly to the north of the Nyagrodha tree and to the south of Keśava.
One should dwell in that palace, for it is indeed composed of Dharma; having seen that image there, which was fashioned by the Lord himself. (70)
"Indeed, those men go to my abode without any exertion;
however, once while he was going along, the King of Dharma himself beheld him. (71)
Having approached my presence and bowed his head, he said:
"Homage to you, O Blessed One, O God, Lord of the World, the Embodiment of Splendor! (72)
To the god who dwells in the ocean of milk, who reclines upon the vast body of Śeṣa, the most excellent, the most worthy of choice, the giver of boons, the creator, the imperishable Lord. || 73 ||
[He saw] Viṣṇu, the Lord of All, the unborn, the omniscient, the unconquered, dark as the petal of a blue lotus, with eyes like white lotuses. || 74 ||
All-pervading, devoid of qualities, tranquil, the sustainer of the universe, the unmanifest creator of all worlds, the lord of the world who brings happiness. || 75 ||
The ancient Person, the object of knowledge, both manifest and unmanifest, eternal,
existing from of old, the creator, the sacred ford of the world, and the teacher of the universe.
He is endowed with the Śrīvatsa mark upon his chest, adorned with a forest garland,
clad in yellow garments, four-armed, and bearing the conch, the discus, and the mace.
Adorned with necklaces and armlets, wearing a crown and bracelets, endowed with all auspicious marks, yet devoid of all sense organs. || 78 ||
Unchanging, immovable, subtle, consisting of the nature of light, eternal, free from existence and non-existence, all-pervading, and beyond primordial nature (prakṛti). || 79 ||
"I bow to that Lord of the World, the Sovereign, the Bestower of Happiness, the Master"—thus did Dharmarāja formerly speak in the presence of the Nyagrodha tree. (80)
Having praised him with various kinds of hymns, he then prostrated himself;
and seeing him thus bowed down, O illustrious lady, standing with palms joined in reverence— || 81 ||
"O Goddess, I have asked Antaka, the mighty-armed son of Vivasvat, for the reason behind this hymn; for you are composed of all the gods."
For what purpose did he praise [you] in this manner? Tell me that in brief. (83)
Yama said:
In this sacred abode, renowned as Puruṣottama,
an image made of sapphire (indranīla) that fulfills all desires has been fashioned.
O lotus-eyed one, having seen her with single-minded devotion and faith, men who are free from desire go to the world named Śveta. || 85 ||
Therefore, O slayer of enemies, I am unable to perform this task;
be gracious, O Mahādeva, and withdraw this image, O All-pervading Lord! (86)
Having heard these words of Vaivasvata, I said to him:
"Yama, I shall conceal this with sand on all sides."
Then, O Goddess, that image was so concealed by creepers that men desiring heaven could not see it there. (88)
Having covered it with creepers and divine coverings of gold,
he dispatched Yama toward that city in the southern direction.
Then, in that excellent and meritorious field, the renowned Puruṣottama, there was indeed a concealed image made of sapphire.
The Lord Janārdana, the God of gods, related to him in the past everything that had occurred in that event.
The journey of Indradyumna, the sight of the sacred field, the description of that field, and its wonderful manifestation, O enchanting one. (92)
Therein is the account of the vision of Baladeva and especially of Kṛṣṇa, as well as that of Subhadrā, and the majesty of all these in every respect.
The vision of Narasiṃha and likewise the proclamation of his prosperity;
the vision of Ananta-Vāsudeva and the glorification of his qualities. || 94 ||
The greatness of Śvetamādhava, the description of Svargadvāra, the sight of the ocean, as well as the ritual bathing and the libations; || 95 ||
The greatness of bathing in the ocean, as well as that of Indradyumna,
the fruit of the five sacred fords, and likewise the great Jyaiṣṭhī festival.

That Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) previously described to her the truth regarding the bathing of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, as well as the fruit of all pilgrimages, and further described Viṣṇuloka and the sacred field himself.
Thus ends the fifty-second chapter, titled "The Greatness of Puruṣottama," within the dialogue between Vasu and Mohinī in the latter part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa. || 52 ||
Then the fifty-third chapter begins.
Mohinī said:
"O tiger among sages, tell me that ancient matter which I ask about."
Just as those images were previously fashioned by Indradyumna. || 1 ||
O Brahmin, tell me all of that—by what manner was Mādhava pleased with him? I have a great curiosity to hear it. || 2 ||
Vasu said:
Listen, O lady of beautiful eyes, as I relate this ancient account, equal to the Vedas, concerning past events and the origin of images.
When the great sacrifice had commenced and the palace was completed, he then became occupied day and night with the thought of providing an image.
By what means, O Lord of Gods, may I behold the Supreme Person, the illuminator of all worlds, the creator of the origin, the maintenance, and the end? || 5 ||
Overcome by anxiety, the lord of men neither sleeps thus day or night,
nor enjoys various pleasures, nor does he perform bathing or personal adornment.
Images of Viṣṇu on this earth— whether made of stone, wood, or metal— that are endowed with all the auspicious characteristics are worthy of worship.
"Among these three, that which is beloved and worshipped by the gods brings joy when established"; thus he became intent on reflection. || 8 ||
Having worshipped Puruṣottama according to the ritual of the Pañcarātra,
the protector of the earth, overcome with anxiety, began to offer praise.
Indradyumna said:
O Vāsudeva, salutations to you; salutations to you, the cause of liberation. Protect me, O Lord of all worlds, from the ocean of birth and worldly existence. || 10 ||
O you who resemble a stainless silken garment, salutations to you, O Supreme Person;
O Saṅkarṣaṇa, salutations be to you, protect me, O Supporter of the Earth! 11.
Salutations to you who are filled with gold; salutations to you whose banner bears the sea-monster;
salutations to you, O beloved of Rati; protect me, O destroyer of Śambara.
Salutations to you, who resemble a cloud; salutations to you, who are affectionate toward your devotees.
O Aniruddha, let there be salutations to you; protect me and become the granter of boons. || 13 ||
Salutations to you, O abode of the wise; salutations to you, O beloved of the wise;
O Nārāyaṇa, may there be salutations to you; protect me who have come to you for refuge. || 14 ||
Salutations to you, the best among the strong; salutations to you whose weapon is the plow;
salutations to you, the foremost of the wise; salutations to you, born from the lotus.
O four-armed sustainer of the world, protect me, O Great-grandfather!
Salutations to you who have the luster of a dark cloud; salutations to you who are worshipped by the thirty gods.
Save me, O Viṣṇu, Lord of the World, who am submerged in the ocean of existence; salutations to you, O destroyer of the sons of Diti, who resemble the fire of universal destruction! 17.
O Narasiṃha of great heroism, O flaming-eyed one, protect me,
just as in the past the earth submerged in the waters was lifted up from the netherworld.
Likewise, O Great Boar, protect me from the ocean of suffering;
O Kṛṣṇa, the forms of your body that grant boons have been praised by me. (19)
And you, O Lord of Gods, along with these Baladeva and others, exist in separate forms; likewise, O Lord, Garuḍa and the others are your limbs.

O Acyuta, the guardians of the quarters along with their weapons, Vāsava and the others, as well as whatever other manifestations of yours have been described by the wise, O Lord of Gods—[all these are present]. (21)
O Lord of the World, those with large, gracious eyes—all of them, whoever have been worshipped and praised, as well as all of you, have likewise been saluted. || 22 ||
"Grant me a boon that bestows dharma, kāma, artha, and mokṣa; for those divisions of yours, such as Saṅkarṣaṇa and the others, have been proclaimed, O Hari. (23)
Since they are connected with the purpose of your worship, they are therefore dependent upon you;
O Lord of Gods, in the ultimate sense, no distinction exists for you. (24)
Your various forms are merely attributed to you through conventional designation; how can a human being speak of duality in You, who are non-dual? (25)
For you alone, O Hari, are all-pervading, of the nature of consciousness, and untainted; your supreme form is devoid of both existence and non-existence.
Untainted, stainless, subtle, immutable, immovable, and eternal; liberated from all limiting adjuncts, it abides as pure existence alone. || 27 ||
"Even the god [Brahmā] does not know that; O Lord, how then could I know it?
Furthermore, what is your form—clothed in yellow garments and four-armed? || 28 ||
Holding a conch, a discus, and a mace in his hands, wearing a crown and armlets, endowed with the Śrīvatsa mark upon his chest, and adorned with a forest garland. || 29 ||
Therefore, O God, best among all the gods and granter of fearlessness to your devotees, the wise and others who take refuge in you worship you. (30)
Save me, O lotus-eyed one, for I am submerged in the ocean of sense-objects; I see no other refuge in the world, O Lord of the World, to whom I might go for protection. (31)
O Beloved of Kamalā, O Madhusūdana, be gracious toward me; for apart from you, I am beset by hundreds of old age and diseases and oppressed by manifold sufferings. (32)
Filled with joy and sorrow, deluded and tightly bound by the fetters of karma,
I have fallen into this most terrible and dreadful ocean of saṃsāra.
In this ocean difficult to cross due to the waters of sense-objects, agitated by passion and hatred, deep with the whirlpools of the senses, and crowded with the waves of craving and grief; (34)
O Lord, deluded by illusion, I have wandered for a very long time in that which is without support, without foundation, devoid of essence, and utterly fickle.
Being born again and again among thousands of different species,
I have experienced many thousands and tens of thousands of births.
O Janārdana, various things have been experienced by me in this saṃsāra; I have studied the Vedas along with their auxiliary limbs and various treatises. (37)
The Itihāsas and Purāṇas, as well as numerous crafts; discontentments and contentments, many accumulations and expenditures. (38)
O Lord of the World, I have experienced the separations and reunions of wives, friends, and my own kinsmen—experiences that are neither subject to decay nor increase. (39)
Various fathers and mothers have been seen by me in that way, and many sorrows as well as many joys have been experienced by me. (40)
Relatives, sisters, brothers, and kinsmen have arrived; likewise, I have dwelt within the womb of women, which is slippery with feces and urine. (41)
O Lord, great suffering was experienced during residence in the womb, as well as the many sufferings in childhood and those arising from the pride of youth. (42)
And in old age, O Hṛṣīkeśa, those very sufferings which exist at death in the hidden path of Yama’s abode have indeed been attained by me. (43)
I have experienced those torments in the hell crowded with agonies—
those of worms, insects, trees, elephants, horses, deer, and birds.
[He was born] in the wombs of buffaloes, cows, and likewise other forest-dwellers, as well as in the wombs of all the twice-born and of Śūdras. || 45 ||
Of the wealthy and of the Kṣatriyas, of the poor and of ascetics, of kings and of royal servants, as well as of other embodied beings. || 46 ||
O Lord, I have been born again and again in their homes, and I have repeatedly fallen into the state of servitude to many human beings as their slaves. (47)
"I was poor, yet I attained sovereignty and lordship; 'I have killed,' 'he has been killed by others,' 'it was killed by me,' or 'he was caused to be killed by me. (48)
"I have given to others, and I have been given by others on many occasions; and I have given for the sake of my father, mother, circle of friends, and wife. (49)
At times joyful and at other times overcome by wretchedness with a face washed by tears, I have gone among gods, animals, humans, and all things moving and stationary.
O Lord, there is no place where I have not gone; O Master of the World, when was my dwelling in hell, and when was it in heaven? (51)
Sometimes in the worlds of humans, sometimes among the animal realms, sometimes in a water-wheel, likewise on a potter’s wheel, and sometimes bound in a well. || 52 ||
"O best of gods, when have I ever remained in the middle? Likewise, I am merely clinging to the creeper of karma. (53)
Thus, in this wheel of saṃsāra, which is terrifying and hair-raising, I have wandered for a very long time and never see its end. || 54 ||
O Hari, I do not know what I should do; my senses are agitated, I am overwhelmed by grief and thirst, bewildered as to where to go, and deprived of my wits.
Now, O Lord, I have come to you for refuge, rendered helpless;
protect me, O Kṛṣṇa, for I am suffering and submerged in the ocean of worldly existence. (56)
Have mercy, O Lord of the World, if you consider me a devotee; for apart from you, I have no kinsman who will care for me. (57)
O Lord, having obtained you as my protector, I have no fear anywhere—neither regarding life nor death, nor concerning security and well-being, O Master. (58)
But as for those lowest of men, O God, who do not worship you according to the prescribed rule—how can there be a happy rebirth for them from the bondage of saṃsāra? (59)
Of what use is their lineage, conduct, learning, or even life to those in whom devotion toward Keśava, the sustainer of the world, does not arise? (60)
But those who, having fallen into a demonic nature and being deluded, revile you, fall into a terrible hell, being born again and again. || 61 ||
O Lord, there is no deliverance for those wicked men, the lowest of humanity, who defile you; they shall not emerge from that ocean of hell. || 62 ||
In whatever birth I may be born due to the bondage of my karma, O Hari, may there always be unimpaired devotion toward you in each of those lives. (63)
Having propitiated you, O Supreme One, the Daityas and other men who have come together have attained the highest perfection; O God, who would not worship you? (64)
Even Brahmā and the other gods are unable to praise you, who transcend primordial nature; yet, O Lord, you have been praised by me according to my state of ignorance.
Therefore, forgive my offenses if you have any compassion for me;
O Hari, even toward one who has committed an offense, the virtuous grant forgiveness. (66)
Therefore, O Lord of Gods, be gracious, having resorted to affection out of devotion;
for you have been praised by me, O God, with a mind full of the sentiment of devotion.
May all that be complete with its constituent parts; O Vāsudeva, salutations be unto you! || 68 ||
Thus ends the fifty-third chapter, titled "The Majesty of Puruṣottama," within the dialogue between Vasu and Mohinī in the latter portion of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa. || 53 ||
Now begins the fifty-fourth chapter.
Vasu said: Thus praised by him at that time, the one whose banner is Garuḍa became pleased.
But he granted her everything desired by her heart, O fortunate lady.
The wise man who, having fully worshipped the Lord of the World, praises Him every day with this hymn, certainly attains liberation. || 2 ||
The wise man who, being pure, recites this supreme hymn at the three junctions of the day,
shall obtain virtue, wealth, pleasure, and liberation.
Whoever should read it, or even hear it, or cause it to be heard with a concentrated mind, shall go to the eternal world of Viṣṇu, their impurities completely shaken off.
This auspicious [work] is blessed, a destroyer of sins, and bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
it is secret, very difficult to obtain, and meritorious, and should not be given to just anyone.
One should never give this to an atheist, a fool, an ungrateful person, one who is conceited, one of wicked intellect, or one who lacks devotion.
It should be given to one endowed with devotion, possessed of virtuous qualities and good character, a devotee of Viṣṇu, peaceful, and habituated to faithful practice.

This most excellent hymn of Puruṣottama has been spoken by me; it is the cause for the destruction of all sins, known as Compassion, the bestower of blissful liberation, and the grantor of the fruits of every desire.

Those who constantly meditate upon that ancient Person, who is exceedingly subtle and whose garment is the stainless sky, attain liberation and enter Viṣṇu, just as clarified butter offered with mantras enters the sacrificial fire.
He alone is the God who destroys the suffering of existence; there is no other beyond him, nor any other besides him.
He is the creator, the protector, and the bringer of the end of all; he is Viṣṇu, equal to all and the essence of everything.

Of what use is learning, of what use are their virtuous qualities, and of what use are their sacrifices, gifts, and fierce austerities, for those who possess no devotion here to Kṛṣṇa, the teacher of the world and the bestower of the bliss of liberation? (11)
In this world, he alone is blessed, he alone is pure, he alone is wise, he alone is an eloquent speaker, and he alone is of virtuous character;
he alone is a knower, a donor, and a speaker of truth, who possesses devotion for the one named Puruṣottama.
Having thus praised Vāsudeva, the son of Brahmā, the eternal Lord of the World who bestows the fruits of all desires, he bowed down to him.
Overcome with anxiety, the protector of the earth spread kusha grass upon the ground,
and having laid down his garment, he lay down on the surface of the earth with his mind fixed on that alone.
"How shall Janārdana, the God of gods, come before my very eyes? When will that Lord, who removes my anxiety, appear?"—thus he reflected.
While that king was asleep, Vāsudeva, the teacher of the world and the wielder of the discus, revealed himself to him in a dream.
And in a dream, he beheld that God of gods, the Lord of the universe—
tranquil, bearing the conch and the discus, with a mace and a lotus in his hands.
It was equipped with a Śārṅga bow, arrows, and a sword, possessing a blazing circle of fierce splendor;
it had the hue of the sun at the end of an eon and resembled blue lapis lazuli. || 18 ||
Seeing the Lord seated upon the back of Garuḍa, possessing eight arms, he spoke: "Excellent, O King, O high-minded one! (19)
O protector of the earth, I am pleased with you because of this divine sacrifice as well as your devotion and faith; why do you grieve in vain?
O King, regarding this eternal image which is worthy of royal worship, I shall tell you the means by which you may obtain it, O Lord of the Earth. (21)
When this night has passed and the stainless sun has risen,
at the edge of the ocean's waters, adorned with various trees— || 22 ||
O King, at that very shore, the vast waters of the salt ocean were seen completely overwhelmed by waves.
A great tree clinging to the bank stands both on land and in water; though struck by the tides, it remains firm and does not tremble. || 24 ||
Taking an axe in your hand, go from there into the midst of the reeds; wandering alone, you will see a royal tree. || 25 ||
Having observed this sign, cut down that tall tree of wondrous appearance without hesitation as it is being felled. (26)
"O protector of the earth, having seen that very [image] and reflected upon it, then behold its divine likeness; abandon this deluding anxiety. (27)
Having spoken thus, the illustrious Hari vanished from sight;
and he too, perceiving that dream, was filled with supreme wonder.
Gazing at that night with his mind fixed upon it,
he recited the Vaiṣṇava mantras and the hymn dedicated to Him.
When the night had turned to dawn, Tugata, with his mind focused on nothing else, then bathed properly in the ocean according to the prescribed rite.
Having given gifts to the Brahmins, including villages and cities, and having performed his morning rites, that best of kings departed. || 31 ||
Neither with a chariot nor on foot, neither with an elephant nor with a charioteer, did that lord of the earth enter the great ocean alone. || 32 ||
He beheld that great tree, a radiant and mighty forest monarch,
which was like the Great Destroyer, possessed of great growth, meritorious, yet indeed devoid of fruit.
He was like a great festival, possessed of a massive body, sleeping near the water, with the dense luster of the color of madder, and devoid of name and caste. || 34 ||
Likewise, the lord of men, filled with joy upon seeing the tree of Viṣṇu,
felled it with a sharp and sturdy axe.
The mind of Indra’s friend became divided there;
however, as he gazed at the piece of wood, a wondrous sight appeared.
Both Viśvakarman and Viṣṇu, those two great-souled ones, arrived assuming the forms of brahmins, appearing exactly like members of the twice-born class.
Blazing with great splendors and adorned with divine garlands, perfumes, and unguents,
the two of them then approached that king, the friend of Indra.
They both said, "O Great King, what will you do here? O mighty-armed one, why has this lord of the forest been cut down by you? (39)
Without a companion, in a great hardship, in a desolate and dense forest, and on the bank of a great river, he was indeed felled like a mighty tree. || 40 ||
Having heard their words, O fair-browed one, that king was filled with joy and spoke words that were both gentle and sweet to them.
Seeing those two Brahmins there, who had arrived like the moon and the sun, he bowed to the Lords of the World and stood with his face cast downwards.
"O Lord, it is my intention to fashion an image in order to propitiate the God who is without beginning or end, immeasurable, and the Lord of the universe. (43)
I am he who was pointed out by the supreme Great-Souled God of gods at the end of a dream, and I have now made this known to you.
Having heard those words of Devendra Pratima, Yajña,
the Lord of the Universe, laughed and, being pleased, spoke these words to him.
Excellent, excellent, O protector of the earth, that this mind of yours is so supreme regarding this terrible ocean of worldly existence, which is like the leaf of a plantain tree!
In this world which is essence-less, full of suffering, agitated by desire and anger, turbid with the whirlpools of the senses, difficult to cross, and hair-raising; || 47 ||
Since your mind has indeed been directed toward the propitiation of Viṣṇu, even though this world is characterized by hundreds of whirlpools of various diseases and resembles a flickering bubble.
"Blessed are you, O tiger among kings, adorned with all virtues;
blessed is the earth, along with its subjects, mountains, forests, and cities. (49)
Together with its villages and cities, adorned by the four castes, it is there, O tiger among kings, that you, the lord, protect the subjects.
"Come, come, O illustrious one! Stay with us two upon this tree, which is pleasant and cool, engaged in discourses based on the Dharma. (51)
"This foremost of artisans, equal to Viśvakarman himself, has come to be your companion; he is truly skilled in all crafts. (52)
"He is making an image that was commissioned by me; leave the bank.
Upon hearing these words of the twice-born man, the king then [acted].
Leaving the shore of the ocean and going near it, that best of kings stood in the very cool shade of a tree. || 54 ||
Then that Soul of the Universe spoke to that preeminent artisan, who was born of the Creator, saying, "Fashion it in that form, with that very appearance. (55)
He is of dark form, supremely tranquil, with eyes as broad as lotus petals,
bearing the Śrīvatsa mark and the Kaustubha gem, and holding the conch, the discus, and the mace.
The second [deity] is the god named Ananta, who is fair-complexioned with the luster of cow's milk, marked with the svastika, and bearing the plow as his weapon; he possesses great strength.
Indeed, his end was not known by the gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, vidyādharas, or uragas; therefore he is remembered as Ananta (the Infinite). || 58 ||
And the third was Subhadrā, the sister of Vāsudeva, golden-hued, most beautiful, and endowed with all auspicious marks.
Having heard these words of his, Viśvakarman, the performer of noble deeds,
immediately had images endowed with auspicious marks fashioned.
They were beautifully adorned by their two ears with variegated earrings,
which shone like the sun due to the marks of the discus and the plough impressed upon them.
First, [one should visualize] those of white complexion, with a luster like the autumnal moon, having deep red eyes, a massive body, and a head formidable with its protruding jaw. || 62 ||
He was fierce, wearing blue garments, possessed of wondrous earrings,
divine, bearing a great plow and wielding a massive mace.
The second [form] has lotus-like eyes, resembles a dark blue cloud, is like the color of an *atasī* flower, and has eyes as broad as lotus petals. || 64 ||

[One should meditate upon] Hari, who has the Śrīvatsa mark on his chest, who wears shining yellow garments, who is infallible (Acyuta), whose hands hold the discus and the conch, who is divine, and who removes all sins.
The third [form] has the luster of gold, with eyes as broad as lotus petals,
draped in variegated garments, and adorned with necklaces and armlets.
Viśvakarman fashioned a beautiful woman adorned with various ornaments, draped with a garland of jewels, and possessing full, uplifted breasts.
But that king, having witnessed the marvel, saw in a single moment [beings] created,
clothed in pairs of divine garments and adorned with various jewels.
Having attained the highest wonder at the statues, which were endowed with all the auspicious marks and were most enchanting, he spoke these words: || 69 ||
"Have you both arrived as gods, assuming the forms of twice-born brahmins?
Both of you possess wondrous deeds, divine in conduct, yet human in appearance."
Are you gods or even humans, or perhaps the excellent Yakṣas and Vidyādharas; or are you Brahmā and Viṣṇu, the Vasus, the Rudras, or the Aśvins? || 71 ||
I do not know whether you two are speakers of truth or exist in the form of an illusion; I have come for refuge—speak to me of your true nature.
The twice-born said:
"I am neither a god, nor a yakṣa, nor a daitya, nor the king of the gods;
I am neither Brahmā nor Rudra—know me to be Puruṣottama. (73)
He is the destroyer of the suffering of all worlds, possessed of infinite strength and prowess; indeed, he is to be worshipped by all beings, for his end is not known.
That which is recited in all the scriptures, proclaimed in the Vedantas, and described by yogis as Vāsudeva, who is attainable through meditation; || 75 ||
I alone am Brahmā himself; I am Viṣṇu, and indeed I am Śiva; I am Indra, the king of the gods, and Yama, the restrainer of the world. || 76 ||
The elements beginning with earth, the three sacrificial fires, the consumer of oblations (Agni), Varuṇa as the lord of waters, and I myself am the supporter—the mountains. || 77 ||
Whatever exists in the world as speech, and whatever is in the universe—both stationary and moving—know me to be that universal form; there is nothing whatsoever other than me.
"I am pleased with you, O best of kings, O observer of noble vows; choose a boon.
Whatever is desired and established in your heart, that I shall grant. (79)
The sight of me does not arise even in a dream for those devoid of merit;
you, however, because of your firm devotion, have seen me directly before your eyes. || 80 ||
O King, having heard these words of Vāsudeva, Mohinī’s body became covered with horripilation, and he sang this hymn of praise.
The king said:
"O Beloved of Śrī, salutations to you; O Lord of Śrī, wearer of yellow garments;
O Giver of Śrī, Lord of Śrī, Abode of Śrī, salutations to you, O Dwelling-place of Śrī. (82)
I bow down to the primordial Puruṣa, the Lord, the Master of all, whose face is turned in every direction, the partless, supreme, eternal God. || 83 ||
Beyond sound, beyond qualities, devoid of existence and non-existence, untainted, devoid of attributes, subtle, all-knowing, and the source of all beings. || 84 ||
I bow to the god who bears the conch and the discus, who holds the mace and the club, the boon-granting deity whose complexion is like the petal of a blue lotus. (85)
I bow to Hari, Hṛṣīkeśa, who reclines on the serpent-couch, who dwells in the Ocean of Milk, and who removes all sins.
Once again, O Lord of the gods of gods, I bow to you, the all-pervading bestower of boons, Viṣṇu, the sovereign of all worlds, the imperishable cause of liberation. || 87 ||
Having thus praised that god, having prostrated with palms joined in reverence,
he spoke while bowing down and falling upon the surface of the earth.
"If you are pleased with me, O Lord, I choose this supreme boon:
may the gods, the suras, along with the gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and great serpents [be under my command]. (89)
The Siddhas, Vidyādharas, Sādhyas, Kinnaras, and Guhyakas, as well as the highly fortunate Ṛṣis who are experts in various scriptures; || 90 ||
Those who are devoted to the practice of renunciation, those who contemplate the true nature of the Vedas, and others who know the path to liberation—all these meditate upon the supreme state. (91)
Through your grace, I desire to attain that state which is stainless, devoid of qualities, and peaceful, which the wise behold, yet which is so very difficult to reach. (92)
The Blessed Lord said:
"May all be well with you; may everything be as you desire.
By my grace, it shall come to pass exactly according to your wish; of this there is no doubt."
"O best of kings, rule over a great kingdom for ten thousand and nine hundred years without interruption."
Having attained that supreme, divine state—difficult for even gods and asuras to reach—which fulfills all desires, is peaceful, secret, unmanifest, and imperishable. || 95 ||
Higher than the highest, subtle, untainted, devoid of qualities, eternal, liberated from thought and sorrow, and free from action and its cause. || 96 ||
Therefore, I shall show you that supreme state known as the "knowable";
having attained it, you will reach supreme bliss and the highest goal. || 97 ||
And may your fame, O Indra among kings, endure upon this earth as long as the earth and the sky exist, and as long as the moon, the sun, and the stars remain. || 98 ||
As long as the seven oceans exist, as long as Mount Meru and the other mountains remain, and as long as the gods abide in heaven, so long shall you remain everywhere immutable. (99)
There is a sacred ford named Indradyumna-saras, originating from the sacrificial clarified butter;
having bathed there even once, a person shall attain the world of Śakra.
Whoever shall offer a funeral ball (piṇḍa) on this auspicious shore of the ocean,
having delivered twenty-one generations of his lineage, shall go to the world of Śakra.
Honored by Apsarases and by Gandharvas with the sounds of their songs, he shall travel there in a celestial chariot for as long as the reigns of fourteen Indras endure.
To the south of the lake, situated in the southwest direction, there is a banyan tree; near it is a pavilion.
Covered by groves of *ketakī* trees and crowded with various kinds of trees,
[it was situated] on the fifth day of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, under the constellation presided over by the ancestors (Maghā).
They will lead us there under the constellation Ṛkṣa; having taken us there, they will indeed keep us for seven days in a pavilion with beautiful courtesans and splendid ornaments.
With various kinds of diversions, enchanting dances and songs, fly-whisks with golden handles, fans, and ornaments of precious gems. || 106 ||
Then those supreme women will stand before us, manifesting [their forms],
as well as celibate students, ascetics, and the best of the twice-born who have completed their ritual baths.

Forest-dwellers, householders, perfected ones, and other twice-born men [praised him] with hymns consisting of various syllables and words, and with the sounds of the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas. || 108 ||
O King, they will again offer praise to Rāma and Keśava; then, having praised them, beheld them, and bowed down with devotion, [they shall attain their goal]. || 109 ||
That man shall dwell for ten thousand divine years in the glorious city of Hari,
being honored by Apsaras and by Gandharvas with the sounds of their songs.
There, indeed, the follower of Hari sports with Keśava.
Resplendent with a celestial chariot the color of the sun and adorned with necklaces of jewels,
O highly fortunate lady, all objects of desire abide within this supreme abode.
Having returned here due to the exhaustion of his merit from asceticism, a man shall become a Brāhmaṇa;
he will certainly become a glorious lord of ten million in wealth and a master of the four Vedas. || 113 ||
Having thus granted him the boon and established the agreement, O blessed lady, Hari vanished from sight along with Viśvakarman.
Then that king, thrilled and with the hair on his body standing on end, considered himself as one who had accomplished his purpose through the sight of Hari.
Then [he saw] Kṛṣṇa, Rāma, and Subhadrā, the bestower of boons,
on chariots resembling celestial palaces and adorned with jewels and gold.
Then, after those sounds of victory and auspiciousness had been sounded,
the wise king, together with his ministers and his domestic priest, led them [the bridegroom and his party] inside.
Having established [the image] in an auspicious, pure, and very beautiful place, amidst the sounds of various musical instruments and the auspicious chanting of the various Vedas. || 118 ||
Then, on an auspicious lunar day, under his own asterism, at a time marked by favorable signs,
he performed the consecration ceremony together with the twice-born at an excellent moment.
Having performed everything according to the prescribed method and the ritual seen in the injunctions, with the approval of the preceptor, the lord of the earth [acted]. (120)
Then the Lord, having duly given the sacrificial fee to the preceptor,
likewise gave wealth to the officiating priests and to others according to the prescribed rules.
Having performed the consecration according to the rules in that most excellent palace,
he installed all those [images] fashioned by Viśvakarman.
Then, having worshipped according to the prescribed rite with various fragrant flowers, gold, gems, pearls, and other such items, as well as various beautiful garments; || 123 ||
He gave provinces, cities, and towns to the twice-born;
having thus bestowed many kinds of gifts and ruled the kingdom as was appropriate. (124)
Having performed various sacrifices and given gifts many times over,
the king, having fulfilled his purpose and renounced all possessions,
went to that supreme abode, the highest step of Viṣṇu.
Thus ends the fifty-fourth chapter, titled "The Majesty of Śrī Puruṣottama," within the dialogue between Mohinī and Vasu in the latter portion of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa. || 54 ||
Now begins the fifty-fifth chapter.
Mohinī said:
"O best of the twice-born, at what time should one go to Puruṣottama?"
O giver of honor, by what rite should even the five sacred fords (pañcatīrthī) be performed?
And tell me, one by one, the specific fruit that comes from bathing and giving gifts at each individual sacred ford (tīrtha), as well as from beholding the deities. || 2 ||
Vasu said:
"He who, having conquered his senses and subdued his anger, should perform penance at Kurukṣetra for ten thousand years with only one foot raised and without food;"
Having observed a fast and beheld Puruṣottama even once on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Jyeṣṭha, one obtains a fruit even greater than that.

Therefore, O auspicious one, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) should be visited with great effort and self-restraint by mortals who desire the heavenly world when he is in his most exalted state. || 5 ||
Having duly performed the Pañcatīrthī rite during the month of Jyeṣṭha, the best of men should behold that Puruṣottama on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight.
Those who behold the imperishable God, Puruṣottama, on the twelfth day, reach the world of Viṣṇu and never fall from it again.
Therefore, O daughter of Vidhi, one should go with great effort to Jyeṣṭha;
having duly performed the pilgrimage to the five sacred fords (pañcatīrthī), Puruṣottama is to be beheld.
Even if situated far away, one who is pure in soul and joyful in spirit should chant the praises of Puruṣottama day after day; such a person shall also go to the city of Viṣṇu.
The man who, being composed and endowed with faith, undertakes a pilgrimage to Kṛṣṇa, shall be liberated from all sins and go to the world of Viṣṇu.
Upon seeing the discus of Hari situated atop the palace from afar,
a man who bows down to it with devotion is instantly liberated from sin.
I shall describe the ritual of the five holy fords (pañcatīrthī); listen, O Mohinī, until the end, by the performance of which a human being becomes dear to Mādhava. (12)
Having gone to the Mārkaṇḍeya lake and bathed, being pure and facing north, one should immerse oneself there three times and recite this mantra: || 13 ||
Save me, who am submerged in the ocean of saṃsāra, seized by sin, and devoid of consciousness; O Destroyer of Bhaga’s eyes, O Enemy of Tripura, homage be unto you! (14)
Salutations to Śiva, the peaceful one and the remover of all sins;
O Lord of Gods, I perform this bath; may my transgression perish. (15)
Standing in water reaching up to his navel, the wise man should duly gratify the deities, the sages, the ancestors, and others with water mixed with sesame seeds.
Having bathed in this manner and likewise sipped water for purification (ācamana), one should then proceed to the temple of Śiva;
having entered the sanctuary of the deity, one should perform a circumambulation of it three times.
Having worshipped Mārkaṇḍeyeśa with devotion using the root mantra, one should prostrate and ask for forgiveness with the Aghora mantra. || 18 ||
O Three-eyed One, salutations be unto you; salutations to you, O Moon-adorned One!
Protect me, O Lotus-eyed One; O Mahādeva, homage be to you.
Having thus bathed in the Mārkaṇḍeya lake and beheld Śaṅkara,
a human being obtains the fruit of ten horse-sacrifices.
Completely liberated from all sins, he goes to the world of Śiva; having enjoyed excellent pleasures there until the dissolution of all beings, he remains.
Having attained this world, a brahmin who is deeply learned in the scriptures may attain the yoga of Śaṅkara and thereby obtain liberation.
Then, having gone to the Kalpavṛkṣa and having circumambulated it three times, one should worship that banyan tree with supreme devotion using this mantra: || 23 ||
Oṃ, salutations to you of unmanifest form, the Great One, the protector of those who bow;
salutations be to you, Nyagrodha, seated upon the great waters. || 24 ||
O Nyagrodha, you who have always resided at the abode of Hari throughout the kalpa; O Kalpavṛkṣa, remove my sin; salutations be unto you! (25)
Having performed a circumambulation with devotion and having gone to the Kalpavaṭa tree, a man suddenly casts off the flood of his sins, just as a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.
O enchanting one, by stepping upon the shadow of that Kalpa tree, a man may abandon even the sin of killing a Brahmin; what need is there to mention other sins?
Having seen Viṣṇu, who was born from the body of Kṛṣṇa, supreme, consisting of Brahmanic splendor, and having the form of a banyan tree, he prostrated before him at the command of Brahmā.
He obtains even greater fruit than that of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices;
likewise, having uplifted his lineage, he goes to the world of Viṣṇu. || 29 ||
Having paid obeisance to Vainateya, who stands before Kṛṣṇa, one is liberated from all sins and shall thereafter go to the city of Viṣṇu. || 30 ||
Having seen Vaṭa and Vainateya, whoever beholds Puruṣottama, Saṅkarṣaṇa, and Subhadrā, he goes to the supreme goal. || 31 ||
Having entered the sanctuary of Viṣṇu and performed three circumambulations of it, one should worship Saṅkarṣaṇa and Subhadrā with devotion and propitiate them.
Salutations to you, O bearer of the plow; salutations to you, whose weapon is the mace;
salutations to you, beloved of Revatī; salutations to you, who are affectionate toward your devotees. || 33 ||

Salutations to you, O best among the strong; salutations to you, O upholder of the earth; salutations to you, O enemy of Pralamba; may there be salutations to you, O elder brother of Kṛṣṇa; protect me! || 34 ||
Thus he propitiated the infinite and unconquerable one, worshipped by the thirty gods,
whose form was like the peak of Mount Kailāsa and whose face was as beautiful as the moon.
The god wears blue garments, his head made formidable by a hooded serpent, possesses great strength, holds a plow, and is adorned with a single earring. || 36 ||
A person who worships Rauhineya with devotion shall obtain his desired fruit;
liberated from all sins, he goes to the world of Viṣṇu. || 37 ||

Having enjoyed [the fruits of his merit] there until the dissolution of all elements (ābhūtasamplava), that wise one, the most excellent among yogins, returns here upon the exhaustion of his merit into a family of yogins.
Having become a preeminent Brāhmaṇa and having mastered the meaning of all the scriptures, one attains knowledge therein and achieves liberation, which is difficult to obtain. || 39 ||
Having thus worshipped Balarāma, the wise man, being well-composed, should then worship Kṛṣṇa with the twelve-syllable mantra.
Those wise ones who always worship Puruṣottama with devotion by means of the twelve-syllable mantra indeed attain liberation. || 41 ||
Neither the gods, nor the practitioners of yoga, nor even the drinkers of Soma reach that goal which those born of ritual action attain when they are devoted to the twelve-syllable mantra. 42.
Therefore, having worshipped Kṛṣṇa, the teacher of the world, with devotion using that very mantra and offerings such as perfumes and flowers, one should prostrate and seek his grace. || 43 ||
Victory to you, O Kṛṣṇa, Lord of the Universe! Victory to you, destroyer of all sins! Victory to you, slayer of Cāṇūra and Keśin! Victory to you, annihilator of Kaṃsa! || 44 ||
Victory to you, O lotus-petal-eyed one! Victory to you, O wielder of the discus and mace! Victory to you, O dark as a blue cloud! Victory to you, O bestower of all happiness! 45.
Victory, O God, worshipful to the world! Victory, O destroyer of saṃsāra!
Victory, O Lord of the worlds, O Protector! Victory, O bestower of the fruits of desire! 46.
In the terrible ocean of saṃsāra—essenceless, with suffering for its foam, fierce with its multitude of crocodiles that are anger, and flooded with the waters of the sense-objects. (47)
O best of gods, O Supreme Person, I am submerged in this ocean agitated by the waves of various diseases and difficult to cross due to the whirlpools of delusion; save me! 48.
Thus having propitiated the Lord of Gods— the giver of boons, compassionate toward his devotees,
the god who removes all sins and bestows the fruits of all desires— || 49 ||

He had broad shoulders, two arms, and was dark-complexioned; his eyes were as long as lotus petals, his chest was wide, and he had mighty arms; he wore yellow garments and possessed a beautiful countenance. || 50 ||
Holding a conch, a discus, and a mace in his hands, adorned with a crown and armlets, endowed with all auspicious marks, and decorated with a forest garland. || 51 ||
O Mohinī, having seen [her], a man who joins his palms in reverence and prostrates like a staff attains the fruit of thousands of horse-sacrifices.
Whatever fruit is proclaimed for bathing and giving gifts at all sacred fords, a man obtains that same fruit by beholding Kṛṣṇa and bowing down to him.
