having enjoyed various kinds of happiness there with joy for sixty kalpas.
At its end, that man shall go to the wondrous abode of Śakra; having arrived there, he shall enjoy happiness for fifty kalpas.
He enters divine abodes adorned with celestial chariots, and having enjoyed exceedingly rare pleasures for a duration of forty kalpas. || 92 ||
He does not come to the world of the stars, which is endowed with manifold happiness; having enjoyed excellent pleasures there for thirty kalpas as he desires, [he attains liberation].
Therefore, he goes to that world where Soma, the son of Viriñci, dwells, adorned by all the gods. || 94 ||
Having enjoyed there for twenty kalpas a pleasure that is very difficult to obtain,
he then goes to the world of Āditya, which is honored by the gods.
Having enjoyed auspicious pleasures there for ten kalpas in perfect peace, he then comes from that place to the exceedingly rare abode of the Gandharvas.
Having enjoyed all pleasures there at his ease for one kalpa, he returns to the earth and becomes a righteous king.
The universal monarch, possessed of great heroism and adorned with all virtues, having ruled the kingdom righteously and performed sacrifices accompanied by liberal gifts, [attained this state]. (98)
At the end of that, having gone to the auspicious world of the Yogins which bestows liberation, he shall enjoy excellent pleasures there until the dissolution of all beings.
Therefore, having returned here once more, he is born into a family of yogins. || 100 ||
O virtuous lady, there was an excellent Brahmin, a master of the four Vedas, devoted to the sacrifice to Brahman, who was noble, auspicious, difficult to find, and esteemed by the wise. || 101 ||
Having attained the Vaiṣṇava yoga, one shall obtain the liberation of absolute isolation (kaivalya); thus has the fruit of the pilgrimage to Śrī Puruṣottama been declared to you. (102)
It bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation upon men; what else do you wish to hear?

Thus ends the sixty-first chapter, titled "Description of the Fruit of the Pilgrimage to Puruṣottama-kṣetra," in the section concerning the dialogue between Vasu and Mohinī within the latter part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa, specifically regarding the majesty of Puruṣottama-kṣetra.
Now begins the sixty-second chapter.
Vasiṣṭha said:
O protector of the earth, having heard this, Mohinī, the daughter of Vidhi, [spoke].
The majesty of Puruṣottama bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation. || 1 ||
Mohinī asked that brahmin, her own domestic priest Vasu, once again:
"O brahmin, I have heard the most wonderful account concerning the birth of Puruṣottama."
O observer of noble vows, now speak also of the majesty of Prayāga;
O Guru, I have previously heard that the king of holy places is named Prayāga.
O twice-born one, tell me its greatness, along with the rules for the performance of pilgrimage to those venerable and distinguished sacred sites.
O King, having heard those words spoken by Mohinī regarding that which must be performed according to the rules by men devoted to dharma, that twice-born man—
Preceded by general instructions, Vasu spoke that narrative concerning Prayāga.
Vasu said:
"Listen, O blessed lady, I shall explain the procedure for visiting the sacred fords."
Relying upon which a person may obtain the aforementioned fruit,
the meritorious visiting of sacred fords (tīrthas) excels even sacrifices.
Without fasting for three nights and without visiting sacred fords, a man is born poor even if he has given neither gold nor cows.
By performing sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma with abundant sacrificial fees,
one does not obtain that fruit which is gained by visiting sacred fords (tīrthas).
Even he who, out of ignorance, should visit these sacred fords in this world, becomes fulfilled in all his desires and is glorified in the heavenly realm.
He always obtains a dwelling-place abounding in wealth and grain;
filled with sovereignty and knowledge, he is forever possessed of enjoyments. || 11 ||
By him whose hands, feet, and mind are well-restrained, his fathers and great-grandfathers have been delivered from hell.
Possessing knowledge, austerity, and fame, he enjoys the fruit of sacred pilgrimage sites— he who has desisted from accepting gifts and is content with whatever comes to him.
Free from egoism, he shall obtain the fruit of the sacred fords— he who is free from ritual constructs, free from worldly undertakings, moderate in diet, and has conquered his senses.
Freed from all attachments, that wise man, being faithful and composed, shall partake in the fruit of the sacred fords as he visits them. (15)
One who has committed sin shall indeed be purified; how much more so one who performs pure deeds?
But one who lacks faith, who is afflicted by evil, an atheist, and whose doubts are not severed—[is not purified]. (16)
These five, being intent on the cause [of their own merit], do not partake in the fruit of the sacred ford;
yet for men who have committed sins, there shall be the pacification of that sin at the sacred ford. || 17 ||
A sacred ford (tīrtha) bestows the fruits as described for men of pure soul; he who enters a sacred ford having conquered desire, anger,
and greed shall have nothing unattained through that pilgrimage.
Those wise men who wander among the sacred fords according to the prescribed rule, enduring all pairs of opposites, go to heaven. || 18 ||

Fish dwell at sacred fords such as the Gaṅgā, and flocks of birds reside in temples; yet, being devoid of pure intention, they do not obtain the fruit of those preeminent sacred fords and shrines. (19)

Then, having placed one's being within the lotus of the heart, one should, with a concentrated mind, resort to the sacred fords (tīrthas); for that pilgrimage which has been described by the lords of sages is truly accomplished when performed, undertaken, or even approved.

The student, being well-restrained and duly appointed by his teacher, performs that rite according to the rules; even in the event of the loss of all his possessions, or when his means are meager, he proceeds by placing the Brahmins at the very forefront.
Or else, even when his entitlement to perform sacrifices has ceased, a Brahmin should wander among sacred fords (tīrthas),
because the lords of sages of pure nature have declared that the fruit of sacrifice is fully obtained at sacred fords.
For one who possesses the qualification for *iṣṭi* sacrifices, the home and all the duties of domestic life are preferable;
thus, for one established in the householder stage (*gṛhasthāśrama*), travel to sacred pilgrimage sites (*tīrtha*) was forbidden by those of old.
Some even say that all sacred sites are not equal to the *agnihotra* sacrifice.
Whoever should go on a pilgrimage to sacred sites, being well-restrained, having first established his residence at home, pure and vigilant, should worship Gaṇeśa with devotion and humility.
A wise brahmin, having returned from his journey, should diligently worship the gods, the ancestors, and virtuous brahmins according to his financial means, just as he did before. || 25 ||
For one who acts in this manner, whatever fruit has been described for visiting sacred fords and other such acts shall be attained; there is not even a trace of doubt in this matter. || 26 ||
If one who is traveling to another country performs a Śrāddha with sesame seeds, it is declared to be for the purpose of a journey; this applies equally upon his return, without a doubt. || 27 ||
At Prayāga, during a pilgrimage, or due to the separation from one's father or mother, one should perform the shaving of the hair; one should not remain hairless in vain. || 28 ||
If one is intent on going to Gayā, having performed the śrāddha according to the rules, having donned the dress of a kārpaṭika, and having performed the circumambulation of the village; || 29 ||
Then, having gone to another village, he should eat the remains of the *śrāddha* meal; thereafter, he should go every day, avoiding the acceptance of gifts.
O lady of virtuous vows, for one who travels to the sacred site of Gayā while mounted upon a bull, there shall be the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice at every step as he proceeds.
Indeed, the anger of cows is terrible; for that embodied being, his ancestors dwell in a horrific hell and do not even accept water offerings. || 32 ||
If a man should go by vehicle out of greed for power or out of delusion, that sacred ford (tīrtha) becomes fruitless for him; therefore, one should avoid using a vehicle.
Killing a cow is said to occur when traveling by ox-cart; however, it is fruitless when traveling by horse-carriage.
It would be half as much when traveling by human carriage, and four times that amount when traveling on foot.
Against rain and heat and the like, he should carry an umbrella; on gravel and thorns, desiring protection for his body, he should always walk wearing sandals. (35)
Having reached a sacred ford (tīrtha) by chance and performing a bath there,
one obtains the fruit born of bathing, but not the fruit of a pilgrimage to that sacred ford.
He who goes for the sake of another obtains a sixteenth part [of the merit]; he who goes by chance obtains half the fruit of the sacred site (tīrtha).
One should never examine a Brahmin at sacred fords; Manu has declared that one who arrives there seeking [hospitality] is to be fed. (38)

O Sulocanā, the offering of funeral cakes (piṇḍa) should be made with roasted flour (saktu), or with mixed grain porridge (saṃyāva), or with milk-rice (pāyasa), or even with jujubes (badara), emblic myrobalans (āmalaka), or oil-cake (piṇyāka).

A śrāddha ceremony should indeed be performed there, but it must be devoid of the invocation and the offering of the image; furthermore, it must not be one that has been defiled by the sight of dogs, crows, vultures, or sinners.
The śrāddha performed at sacred fords (tīrtha) is said to bring satisfaction to the ancestors;
likewise, men may perform the tīrtha-śrāddha either out of season or in season. (41)
Once they have arrived there, the libation for the ancestors must always be performed;
no delay should be made, nor should one create any obstacle. || 42 ||
O large-eyed one, whoever should immerse an image made of kusha grass in the waters of a sacred ford, he shall obtain an eighth part of the fruit [of the rite].
"You are Kuśa, the son of Kuśa, fashioned by Brahmā in ancient times; when you have bathed, he for whom this knot-binding is intended has truly bathed. (44)
Shaving the head and fasting— this is the rule at all sacred fords, with the exception of Kurukṣetra, Viśālā, Virajā, and Gayā.
Now hear the reason for the sanctity of terrestrial holy places (tīrthas), just as certain parts of the body are considered most preeminent. (46)
The sanctity of sacred fords (tīrthas) is traditionally held to arise from the marvelous power of the earth, water, and fire, as well as from the acceptance [of these sites] by sages. || 47 ||
O Goddess, whoever reaches the Gaṅgā and does not have their head shaved, all their ritual acts become as if unperformed, and they likewise become an offender against the sacred ford.
He who does not have his head shaved at the Gaṅgā in the field of Bhāskara shall go to the Raurava hell for an eon, accompanied by ten million members of his lineage.
Having reached the Gaṅgā, the best of rivers, the accumulations of sins from the end of the aeon remain clinging to one's hair; therefore, one should avoid them.
For as many thousands of years as there are nails and hairs that fall into the waters of the Ganges, for so long one is glorified in the heavenly world. || 51 ||
However, apart from Prayāga, one must certainly not shave one's head on the Gaṅgā;
he who performs it otherwise out of delusion shall enter the Mahāraurava hell. || 52 ||
He whose father is still living, having reached a sacred ford and knowing the ritual injunctions, should indeed perform the shaving of his head, but not the shaving of his beard.
O Goddess of gods, it is proclaimed by all the sages that even at Gayā and other such places, shaving (kṣaura) is forbidden without first having the beard shaved. || 54 ||
The wise know that shaving along with the beard and hair is "muṇḍana"; O fair-browed one, those who know the Vedas do not declare that a mere haircut is "muṇḍana."

Thus ends the sixty-second chapter, titled "The Ritual for the Sacred Fords," in the section concerning the Great Narration (*Bṛhadupākhyāna*), within the latter part of the *Śrī-Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Vasu and Mohinī, regarding the majesty of Prayāgarāja. || 62 ||
Now begins the sixty-third chapter.
Vasu said:
Listen, O Mohinī, I shall declare the majesty that is in accordance with the Vedas.
Having bathed there according to the prescribed rite of Prayāga, one becomes purified. || 1 ||
The Gaṅgā is equal to Kurukṣetra wherever she is immersed; however, it is said that where she meets with the Vindhya, she is ten times more meritorious than that.
Therefore, the north-flowing [river] at Kāśī is said to be a hundred times superior;
and where it is joined by the daughter of the Sun (the Yamunā), the Gaṅgā is said to be a hundred times superior to that [north-flowing river] at Kāśī.
O Goddess, that western-flowing river becomes a thousandfold more meritorious; by the mere sight of it, she removes even the sin of killing a Brahmin.
The Gaṅgā, flowing westward where it meets the Kālindī, destroys the sins of a hundred kalpas; O Goddess, she is difficult to attain during the month of Māgha.
O blessed lady, that confluence which meets upon the earth in the month of Māgha is called Amṛta; even for the gods, it is difficult to obtain for even a single moment.
Whatever sacred fords and holy cities exist upon the earth,
they all come to bathe in the Veṇī during the month of Māgha when the sun is in Capricorn.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Mahādeva; the Rudras, the Ādityas, and the hosts of Maruts; the Gandharvas, the world-protectors, and the Yakṣas, Kinnaras, and Guhyakas. || 8 ||
Those endowed with the qualities such as *aṇimā* and others, and other seers of reality;
Brahmāṇī, Pārvatī, Lakṣmī, Śacī, Medhā, Aditi, and Rati.
All those wives of the gods, as well as the beautiful women of the nāgas—
Ghṛtācī, Menakā, Rambhā, Urvaśī, and Tilottamā— were there in that auspicious place.
O Virañjika, all the hosts of Apsarases as well as the hosts of Pitṛs come to bathe in the Veṇī during the month of Māgha.
In the Kṛta Yuga they exist in their true form, but in the Kali age all holy places (tīrthas) have become darkened in appearance due to the fault of association with sinners.
They become white in color from bathing at Prayāga during the month of Māgha when the sun is in Capricorn—O Govinda, Acyuta, Mādhava! (13)
"O Lord, by means of this bath, grant me the fruit as it has been described";
having recited this mantra, one should bathe while observing silence. || 14 ||
Furthermore, one should remember Vāsudeva, Hari, Kṛṣṇa, and Mādhava;
for men perform a bath with heated water in his house.
Indeed, that same fruit which is obtained in sixty years is gained when the sun is situated in Capricorn;
moreover, bathing outdoors in a pond or similar body of water is said to yield the fruit of twelve years.
That merit is indeed doubled at a pond, fourfold at a river and the like, tenfold at a natural lake (devakhāta), and a hundredfold at a great river. || 17 ||
That merit of a hundred cycles of four yugas is multiplied a thousandfold at the confluence of two great rivers; all that fruit is obtained when the sun is in Capricorn.
O fair-eyed one, it is proclaimed that by merely bathing in the Gaṅgā at Prayāga,
those who plunge into the Gaṅgā during the month of Māgha [attain the same merit].
O daughter of Brahmā, those who perform this in the month of Māgha do not fall from the abode of the gods for a thousand times four yugas multiplied by a hundred.
The Lord of Creatures ordained this bath at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, as taught by the sages, for the burning away of the mass of sins that is a burden upon the earth.
O Goddess, out of a desire for the welfare of living beings, I established Prayāga as this perfect place for bathing, where the white and black waters meet. 22.
Indeed, for the sake of the sacrificial animals that are of sinful form, Brahmā created in ancient times that stream which is both white and black, interwoven with the Sarasvatī.
The Creator of the world indeed fashioned that path to the realm of Brahmā;
Māgha, the bestower of knowledge, is so, but he does not grant the fruit of liberation.
In the sacred fords on the slopes of the Himalayas, he is declared by the knowers of the Vedas to be the destroyer of all sins and the bestower of Indra’s world;
indeed, Māgha is the best of all months, granting liberation in the forest of Badarī.
The month of Māgha, celebrated on the Narmadā, is proclaimed as the destroyer of sin, the remover of suffering, the bestower of the fruits of all desires, and the giver of the world of Rudra.
The month of Māgha, which destroys the flood of worldly existence, bestows happiness upon all the worlds, and grants abundant fruit, is proclaimed as most excellent at Viśālā. || 27 ||
The Ganges is celebrated as a forest fire for the fuel of sin, as the destroyer of dwelling in the womb, and as the path to the world of Viṣṇu and to liberation. || 28 ||
The Sarayū, Gaṇḍakī, Sindhu, Candrabhāgā, Kauśikī, Tāpī, Godāvarī, Bhīmā, Payoṣṇī, and Kṛṣṇaveṇikā. || 29 ||
A man who bathes in the Kāverī, the Tuṅgabhadrā, and whatever other rivers flow to the ocean, goes to the heavenly world, cleansed of all sin.
In Naimiṣa one attains the same form as Viṣṇu; at Puṣkara, proximity to Brahmā; and by bathing in Māgha at Kurukṣetra, indeed, the world of Ākhaṇḍala (Indra). || 31 ||
O Goddess, by bathing at Devahrada in Māgha—which bestows the fruit of success in yoga—and at Prabhāsa when the sun is in Capricorn, one becomes a member of Rudra’s retinue. || 32 ||
O son of Vidhi, by performing the Māgha bath according to the rules in the Devikā river, one becomes a man with a divine body;
and by bathing in the Gomatī during Māgha, there is no rebirth.
At Hemakūṭa, Mahākāla, Oṃkāra, and likewise at Nīlakaṇṭha and Arbuda, the month of Māgha is considered by Rudra to bestow the worlds.
O Goddess, when the sun is in Capricorn, the full flood of all rivers should be known by the wise as conducive to the attainment of all desires through bathing.
O daughter of the Sun, the month of Māgha is attained at Prayāga by the fortunate, for there the white and black waters grant freedom from rebirth. (36)
The gods dwelling in heaven constantly sing: "Māgha will indeed come to Prayāga for us, where men, having bathed, shall never again enter a womb and shall abide in the presence of Viṣṇu. (37)
In ancient times, the Creator placed Māgha and Prayāga together upon a scale; O daughter of the Four-faced One, of those two, Māgha proved to be the weightier.

Whatever destination men attain through fierce austerities accumulated over a long period— such as emaciating the body by subsisting on air, water, or leaves— and through yogic practices, they indeed attain that same destination by bathing at Prayāga.

For those who have bathed at the holy site of Prayāga, where the celestial river meets [the ocean], at the rising of the sun in the form of a sea-monster (Makara), a swarm of bees, struck by the ears of elephants, adorns the doors of their homes.

How indeed can that Prayāga not be described, which, having effortlessly destroyed all sins, bestows the entire fruit of the great sacrifice known as the Rājasūya resulting from one's ritual bath? (41)
Whatever merit resides in those who are learned in the four Vedas and in those who speak the truth, one obtains that very merit simply by bathing at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Kālindī.
There, one of celebrated vows should perform an ablution at the confluence;
he obtains a fruit equal to that of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices. || 43 ||
The sacred precinct of Prayāga extends five yojanas;
by entering this ground, one performs an Aśvamedha sacrifice at every step.
O fortunate one, there are three pools; by entering Prayāga in their midst, sin is destroyed at that very moment through the Jāhnavī. || 45 ||
A man who bathes at Prayāga for one month with his senses restrained is liberated from all sins, just as was seen by the Self-born One.
But one who is pure, self-restrained, non-violent, and endowed with faith—having bathed—is liberated from sins and shall go to the supreme state. || 47 ||
Naimiṣa and Puṣkara, Gotīrtha and the confluence of the Sindhu and the ocean, Gayā and Dhenuka, and the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean. || 48 ||
These and many other meritorious mountain peaks, as well as ten thousand sacred fords (tīrthas) and thirty crores of others. || 49 ||
Established eternally at Prayāga, the wise ones are ever-increasing;
indeed, the Jāhnavī flows through the midst of those three sacrificial fire-pits.
For having issued forth from Prayāga, preceded by all sacred fords, the goddess who is the daughter of the Sun is renowned throughout the three worlds. (51)
The Yamunā, the purifier of the world, has joined with the Gaṅgā;
that which lies between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā is considered the highest place on earth.
Vāyu has declared that three and a half crores of sacred fords do not equal even a sixteenth part of the holy site of Prayāga.
Those [merits] that exist in heaven, on earth, and in the intermediate space, as well as those in the Ganges— all of them reside at Prayāga, where both Kambala and Aśvatara are established.
Or rather, this is Bhogavatī, the altar of Prajāpati that is to be known;
there, the Vedas and the sacrifices abide in embodied form. || 55 ||
O Satī, the sages whose wealth is austerity worship Prajāpati;
likewise, the gods and the wielders of the discus sacrifice with ritual offerings.
Therefore, O beautiful one, there is nothing more meritorious in the three worlds; by its power, it excels all other sacred fords. || 57 ||
Having seen that supreme site, Prayāga,
there they are liberated from all sins, just as the moon is released by Rāhu.
Then, having gone to Prayāga, which is beheld by all the gods, he dwelt there for a month as a celibate student, propitiating the ancestors and the gods.
One obtains one's desired objects wherever one is attached;
however, even one who is shrouded by hundreds of sins will attain them if they plunge into the white and black [streams].
When the sun is situated in Capricorn during the month of Māgha, he shall not enter a womb again;
for the illusory power of Viṣṇu (vaiṣṇavī māyā) is indeed difficult to conquer, and is hard to abandon even for the gods.
She is indeed burned at Prayāga during the month of Māgha; having enjoyed manifold pleasures in various worlds belonging to Virañci, she [attains liberation].
Thereafter, those who have bathed in Māgha at Prayāga dissolve into the Discus-bearer; he who touches the confluence of the white and dark waters in Māgha when the sun is in Capricorn [attains this].
Even Citragupta is not at all able to calculate the measure of that merit;

the fruit of a thousand Rājasūya sacrifices and a hundred Vājapeya sacrifices certainly accrues to those who bathe in the Sitāsita (the confluence of the white and black rivers) during the month of Māgha. 64.

Whatever sin has been accumulated by human beings over births spanning an entire kalpa, that shall be reduced to ashes for those who bathe at the confluence of the white and dark rivers during the month of Māgha.
The confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā is world-renowned; that very place is a wish-fulfilling holy site (tīrtha), by bathing there with devotion. (66)
Whatever desire anyone may have, that indeed shall be theirs: for one desiring enjoyments there shall be enjoyments, and for one desiring a kingdom there shall be a kingdom.
Heaven shall be attained by one who desires heaven, and liberation by one who desires liberation; whatever holy places there may be in the three worlds that grant all desires, [they are all here].
They all resort to Prayāga when the sun is in Capricorn, as well as to Haridvāra, Prayāga, and the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean. || 69 ||

Having bathed there, O fair-eyed one, one should proceed to the cities of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva; for that bathing at the confluence of the white and dark rivers in the month of Māgha is most meritorious.
One who speaks the truth, has conquered anger, and has taken refuge in non-violence as the supreme practice, does not undergo rebirth even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
One who follows the Dharma, knows the truth, and is devoted to the welfare of cows and Brahmins,
shall be liberated from sin by bathing between the Gaṅgā and Yamunā.
There, one obtains in abundance all the desires conceived by the mind,
as if by giving a thousand bhāras of gold at Kurukṣetra during a solar eclipse.
Whatever fruit one obtains at the Veṇī during the month of Māgha, that same fruit is obtained day by day from the proper gift of a hundred thousand cows.
The fruit obtained by bathing for three days at Prayāga during the month of Māgha is equal to the merit gained through the practice of yoga for three hundred years. (75)
O virtuous one, the fruit that is obtained by bathing for three days at Prayāga during the month of Māgha cannot be attained even by a thousand horse-sacrifices.
In ancient times, Kāñcanamālinī affectionately gave the fruit of bathing for three days during the month of Māgha to a Rākṣasa; by that act, that evildoer was liberated.
The destruction of her sins occurred after three days; having attained divinity through the merit that arose from bathing for twenty-seven days, she reached the state of a goddess.
Delighting on Kailāsa, she became a dear friend of the Daughter of the Mountain; furthermore, by the grace of Prayāga, she came to possess the memory of her former births. || 79 ||
In ancient times, there was a king named Vāsarāja in the region of Avantī;
having reached the sacred site of Narmadā, he performed the Rājasūya sacrifice.
There, with sixteen horses adorned with golden sacrificial posts and richly decorated with golden ornaments, he also shone forth according to the prescribed rite.
Endowed with faith, devoted to the gods, a giver of cows and gold, he bestowed upon the twice-born a mountain-like heap of grain.
"O auspicious one, what [name] is this Brāhmaṇa? He is a fool, of low birth, a farmer of base conduct, and excluded from all religious duties. (83)
Distressed by his labor in the fields and deceived by his kinsmen,
he wandered here and there and departed, tormented by the suffering of being unseen.
Having approached Prayāga by means of divine knowledge,
he bathed there for three days, honoring the great Māghī festival.
That best of the twice-born became sinless merely by bathing; having departed from Prayāga, he went back to the place from which he had come. || 86 ||
Once, when both that king and that brahmin had perished,
their identical destination was seen in the presence of the King of the Gods.
Splendor, beauty, strength, womanly charm, the celestial vehicle, ornaments, a garland of Pārijāta flowers, dance, and song—these were equal for both of them. (88)

Having thus seen the majesty of this sacred field, how could it be said that the Māgha [bath] at the confluence of the white and black waters on the auspicious day is not equal to a Rājasūya sacrifice? (89)
At the confluence of the white and blue waters, twenty bow-lengths wide,
one does not return from Māgha, whereas from the Rājasūya sacrifice one may be reborn.
At the vast bank of the Yamunā, there are the two Nāgas Kambala and Aśvatara;
having bathed and drunk there, one is liberated from all sins. || 91 ||
Having gone there to the abode of the wise Mahādeva,
a man delivers ten ancestors and ten descendants.
And there at Pratiṣṭhāna, there is a well that is exceedingly famous;
having bathed there and offered libations to the ancestors and the gods with a restrained mind, [one attains merit].
The celibate who, having conquered anger, stays here for three nights with his soul purified of all sins, shall obtain the fruit of an Ashvamedha sacrifice.
To the north of Pratiṣṭhāna and to the east of the Bhāgīrathī is the sacred ford named Haṃsapratapana, renowned throughout the worlds.
There, the fruit of an Ashvamedha sacrifice is obtained merely by bathing;
one is honored in heaven for as long as the moon and the sun endure. || 96 ||
Then, having gone to Bhogavatī, to the north of Vāsuki, there is that supreme sacred site (tīrtha) known as Daśāśvamedhika. || 97 ||
Having performed an ablution there, one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice;
he becomes wealthy, handsome, skillful, a donor, and righteous. || 98 ||
Whatever merit is found in the four Vedas, whatever fruit is found in those who speak the truth, and whatever dharma lies in non-violence—the same fruit is obtained from traveling there. || 99 ||
On the northern bank of the Pāyati and on the southern bank of the Prayāga, there is a sacred ford (tīrtha) known as Ṛṇamocanaka, which is remembered as supreme. || 100 ||
Having stayed for one night and bathed, one is liberated from all debts;
one attains the heavenly world and likewise becomes immortal. || 101 ||
He who bathes at the three times of day and practices the renunciation of food shall be purified from the sin of betraying trust within three months.
By chanting [her name] one gains merit; by seeing her one beholds auspicious things;
and by bathing in and drinking from her, one purifies one's lineage up to the seventh generation.
If one does not bathe before sunrise during the month of Māgha when the sun is situated in Capricorn, how can one be liberated from sins, or how can one go to the third heaven? || 104 ||
One should perform the shaving of the head at Prayāga, offer funeral cakes (piṇḍas) in the Gaṅgā, give gifts at Kurukṣetra, and cast off the body at Vārāṇasī. || 105 ||
What is the use of offering funeral cakes at Gayā, or what is the use of dying at Kāśī?
What is the use of giving gifts at Kurukṣetra, if one has undergone the tonsure at Prayāga? (106)
If one should go to a sacred ford again within a year less two months,
one must then diligently perform a tonsure and a fast.
One should prescribe the shaving of the hair for women who have reached Prayāga in this manner:
having pulled out all the hair, one should cut it to a length of two finger-breadths. || 108 ||
All the sins of embodied beings reside at the roots of their hair;
since they depart through bathing at sacred fords, one should therefore have them shaved off here.

If it is conjoined with the asterisms of Aśleṣā, Arka (Kṛttikā), Pāta (Viśākhā), or Śravaṇa during the months of Pauṣa or Māgha, that is to be known as Ardhodaya, which is superior to a hundred solar festivals. || 110 ||
When the rite is performed slightly deficient, it is remembered as "Mahodaya";
this occurs on the seventh day of the bright fortnight of Māgha at the time of dawn. 111.

If one were to obtain [the merit] at Prayāga equal to that of a thousand solar eclipses, the merit at the solstice (ayana) would be ten millionfold, while the fruit at the equinox (viṣuva) would be a hundred thousandfold. || 112 ||
At Ṣaḍaśīti, at the Viṣṇupadīs, and at Prayāga, one should perform acts of giving according to the extent of one's wealth. (113)
O daughter of Vidhi, for one who bestows a cow between the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, the fruit of the sacred ford indeed increases. (114)
O auspicious lady, whoever there offers gold, gems, pearls, or other gifts, as well as a *pāṭalā* or a *kapilā* cow; || 115 ||
Having caused a virtuous Śrotriya to accept, according to the prescribed rite, a milch cow with golden horns, silver hooves, and a cloth around her neck, together with her calf; || 116 ||
To one who wears white garments, who is tranquil, who knows the Dharma, and who has mastered the Vedas—
that cow should be given by her at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā.
And there shall be costly garments and various kinds of jewels as numerous as the pores on the skin of that cow and her calf.
For that many thousands of years he is honored in the heavenly world;
and in whatever place he takes birth, there that cow is born.
And by that deed, the givers do not see hell; having reached Uttarakuru, they rejoice for an inexhaustible time.
One milk-yielding cow is better than a hundred thousand cows;
such a single cow can rescue one's sons, wife, and servants.
Therefore, among all gifts, the gift of a cow is preeminent,
especially when one has entered upon a difficult, treacherous, and terrible path filled with great transgressions.
A cow alone provides protection; therefore, she should be given to the best of the twice-born.
One should not accept [a gift] at a sacred ford, nor at holy shrines.
A twice-born man should indeed remain vigilant regarding all signs,
whether in his own duties, in rites for the ancestors, or even in the worship of the deities.
That sacred ford is fruitless for him as long as he consumes that wealth; however, he who bestows his daughter in marriage between the Gaṅgā and Yamunā [attains its full merit].
He does not see the terrible hell on account of that deed; rather, having gone to the Northern Kurus, he rejoices for an inexhaustible time.
A man obtains righteous sons and wives endowed with beauty;
thereafter, with his head downward and arms raised upward, he should drink smoke.
He is honored in the heavenly world for a hundred thousand years;
having fallen from that heaven, he becomes a man who maintains the sacred fire (agnihotrī). || 128 ||
Having enjoyed abundant pleasures, he returns again to that sacred ford,
extending from Prayāga to Pratiṣṭhāna, as far as my city and the lake of Vāsuki.
The two Nāgas Kambala and Aśvatara [dwell] there; from this Nāga Bahumūlaka, this field of Prajāpati became renowned throughout the three worlds. || 130 ||
Having bathed there, those who die go to heaven and are not born again;
this is known neither from the words of the Vedas nor even from the words of the world.
Indeed, the mind should be directed toward dying at Prayāga, for it is superior to ten thousand holy sites and sixty crores of others.
O daughter of Vidhi, it is proclaimed that their presence is found in that very place which is the destination of the wise man who is established on the true path and endowed with yoga. || 133 ||
That is the destination for a man who gives up his life at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, whether he be oppressed, miserable, or even angry. (134)

He who, having reached the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, should give up his life, [ascends] by means of celestial chariots possessing the brilliance of the sun and the luster of glowing gold. || 135 ||
"The lordly sages declare that a person rejoices in heaven amidst the Gandharvas and Apsarases, obtaining all desired objects. (136)
Awakened by the sounds of singing and musical instruments, he remains honored in heaven for as long as he does not remember his [former] birth. || 137 ||
Then, having fallen from heaven and his karma exhausted, he comes here and is born into a prosperous family filled with gold and jewels.
Constantly recollecting that very place, he goes to the world of Viṣṇu; indeed, he who reaches the foot of the banyan tree and there gives up his life attains that state.
Having transcended all worlds, O Rudra, he goes to the world of Rudra;
there those twelve Ādityas, having taken refuge in Rudra, shine with heat.
The entire world emerges [from it], and at the foot of the banyan tree, Hari, the Blessed One, preceded by Prajāpati, is consumed by fire there.
O Goddess, there on that vast and beautiful sandbank of the Urvaśī river, white as a swan, the infant sits within the fold, sucking his big toe. (142)
Listen also to the fruit for him who gives up his life:
sixty thousand and sixty hundred years.
He shall dwell together with his ancestors in the heavenly world of Brahmā;
and when he beholds Urvashī in the realm of the gods, O fair-eyed one, [he shall attain that state].
He is constantly worshipped by gods, sages, gandharvas, and kinnaras;
then, having fallen from heaven when his merit was exhausted, he has come here.
He shall obtain a hundred beloved women resembling Urvaśī and become the lord of many thousands of women. || 146 ||
O deluder, he who was the ruler and teacher of ten thousand villages is awakened from sleep by the sound of her girdle and anklets. 147.
Having enjoyed abundant pleasures, he attains that sacred ford once again—he who is constantly clad in white garments, self-restrained, and has conquered his senses. (148)
But by eating only once a day for a month, one becomes a master of yoga and obtains a hundred women adorned with golden ornaments. || 149 ||
On this earth, as far as the oceans, he shall become a lord of great enjoyments;
endowed with wealth and grain, he becomes a constant giver. || 150 ||
Having enjoyed abundant pleasures, he remembers that sacred ford again; and whoever, having reached Koṭitīrtha, should give up his life there— || 151 ||
He is honored in the heavenly world for the duration of ten million thousand years;
thereafter, having returned here from heaven once his karma is exhausted, he becomes the best of men. || 152 ||
Whether free from desire or possessed of desire, he who passes away in the Ganges shall be born handsome in a family preeminent for gold, jewels, and pearls. (153)
He attains the heaven of Śakra and does not behold hell; he travels by means of a celestial chariot yoked with swans and cranes. || 154 ||
Surrounded by throngs of Apsarases, he who has fallen asleep there awakens;
having come here from heaven once his karma is exhausted, he becomes a son of Viriñca.
Even for illustrious yogins, he obtains birth according to his own will;
he should maintain a fire of dried cow-dung between the Gaṅgā and Yamunā.
For that wise one was indeed free from missing limbs, free from disease, and endowed with all five senses; yet, upon his body, there were as many pits of greed as there are. (157)
For that many thousands of years he is honored in the heavenly world;
thereafter, having descended from heaven, he becomes the lord of Jambūdvīpa. || 158 ||
Having enjoyed abundant pleasures, he regains that sacred ford once more—he who, having cut off his own body, offers it to the birds. || 159 ||
He is honored in the world of Soma for a hundred thousand years;
thereafter, having returned from there, he becomes a righteous king here on earth. || 160 ||
Endowed with virtues, perfect in form, possessed of learning, pleasant of speech, and pure,
one who has enjoyed abundant pleasures should return once more to that sacred ford.
Within the five-yojana circumference of Prayāga, wherever one may die while observing the vow of fasting unto death, [one attains liberation]. || 162 ||
A man delivers all seven ancestors who have passed away and fourteen descendants yet to come, and he shall uplift himself as well.
The place known as Agnitīrtha is on the southern bank of the Yamunā; however, the tīrtha of Dharmarāja to the west is remembered as Naraka.
Having bathed there, those who die go to heaven and are not subject to rebirth;
furthermore, during the time after the Yamunā, there are many other places that destroy sins.
O knower of rites, there are sacred fords (tīrthas) established by the lords of sages;
those who bathe in them go to heaven, and upon death, they are not born again.
Both the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā are remembered as having equal merit;
yet, solely by virtue of her seniority, the Gaṅgā is worshipped everywhere.
O Goddess of the Gods, for one who bestows all kinds of jewels upon the Brahmins, yoga may or may not be attained through that gift. || 168 ||
For one who dies at Prayāga, all this comes to pass and not otherwise—whether he be staying in his own country, in the forest, in a foreign land, or at home. || 169 ||
Even he who, while merely remembering Prayāga, gives up his life,
attains the world of Brahmā, where the earth is made of gold.
Trees that yield all desired fruits stand there; the sages have departed for the delightful and auspicious bank of the Mandākinī, which is crowded with thousands of women.
He plays with the Siddhas and Gandharvas and is likewise honored by the gods;
then, returning once more to this world, he becomes the lord of Jambudvīpa.
A righteous soul endowed with virtues attains that sacred ford once again;
thus has all this majesty born of Prayāga been recounted to you. || 173 ||
It bestows happiness, it bestows liberation, and it is the essence; what else do you wish to hear? || 174 ||

Thus ends the sixty-third chapter, titled "The Greatness of Prayāga," within the dialogue between Vasu and Mohinī, in the *Bṛhad-upākhyāna* of the latter portion of the glorious *Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa*.
Thus ends the majesty of Prayāga;
now begins the majesty of Kurukṣetra,
being the sixty-fourth chapter.
Mohinī said:
"O compassionate one, knower of dharma, you who are learned in many ways have described to me the greatness of Prayāga, the king of holy places. (1)
Tell me now about Kurukṣetra, which brings auspiciousness among all the foremost of sacred fords (tīrthas) and purifies all the worlds.
Vasu said:
Listen, O Mohinī, I shall describe Kurukṣetra, which bestows great merit;
having gone there and bathed, a person is liberated from all sins. (3)
There, many sacred fords (tīrthas) have been frequented by the lords of sages;
I shall describe them to you, which grant liberation to those who hear of them.
Knowledge of Brahman, performing śrāddha at Gayā, dying during a cattle-raid, and residence in Kurukṣetra—these are said to be the four kinds of liberation for men. || 5 ||
The region between the two divine rivers, the Sarasvatī and the Dṛṣadvatī, which is frequented by the gods, they call Brahmāvarta. || 6 ||
"Even though I am far away, I go to Kurukṣetra and I dwell there"— he who constantly speaks thus is also liberated from sins.
Indeed, the wise person who dwells there, established on the bank of the Sarasvatī, will possess knowledge consisting of Brahman; of this there is no doubt.
The gods, sages, and perfected beings all behold Kurujāṅgala; by frequenting it, O Goddess, one perceives Brahman within the self.
Mohinī said:
O best of the twice-born, how is it that Kurukṣetra is superior to all holy places?
Tell me that in detail; I have come to you for refuge. (10)
Vasu said:
Listen, O blessed lady, I shall describe Kurukṣetra, which yields great fruit, how it was born as the burner of men's sins and is dear to Brahmā. (11)
The meritorious Ādya-Brahmasaras arose in that place;
from there was born Rāmahrada, and after that, Kurukṣetra.
That lake was situated nearby, created by Brahmā in ancient times; and this altar of Brahmā stands within the interior of the region.
O Mohinī, Brahmā performed penance here with the desire for creation, and Hari, the wielder of the discus, performed penance here with the desire for its preservation.
O beautiful lady, even Śambhu attained the state of being a pillar (sthāṇutva) by entering the lake, and Paraśurāma likewise became heated with anger due to the slaughter of his father.
Having gratified with their blood those who had created pools of gore through acts such as the killing of Brahmins and Kshatriyas, he indeed performed penance there.
Then the famous Rāmatīrtha, which destroys all sins, came into being; there, the sage Mārkaṇḍeya performed supreme ascetic penance. || 17 ||
Having arrived there from various places, Sarasvatī, who had originated from the Plakṣa tree,
was honored and praised by that righteous sage.
Having flooded the nearby lake, they set out toward the western direction as far as the field that had been ploughed on all sides by Kuru.
Extending five yojanas in width, with compassion, truth, and forgiveness as its source,
that Syamantapañcaka is declared to be Kurukṣetra itself.
O Goddess, men who bathe here obtain imperishable merit;
and having died, they ascend a celestial chariot and go to the world of Brahmā.
Fasting, giving gifts, burnt offerings, recitation of mantras, and worship of the gods—these indeed attain imperishability; there is no need for deliberation on this point. || 22 ||
Those who die at Kurukṣetra on the Brahmavedī are not subject to rebirth;
yet for the planets, lunar mansions, and stars, there is fear of falling due to the passage of time. (23)
For those who die at Kurukṣetra, there shall be no further falling [into saṃsāra];
the gods, ṛṣis, siddhas, and gandharvas are eager to resort to that lake.
O Goddess, because she was eternally stationed there, that place is known by the name Rantuka; it was established in ancient times by Viṣṇu for the protection of that sacred field.
The yakṣas Sucandra and Sūrya, Vāsuki and Śambukarṇaka, and the vidyādhara Sukeśī were established as auspicious rakṣasas. (26)
Together with their eight thousand attendants, who always carry bows and arrows, they protect Kurukṣetra and ward off the wicked. || 27 ||
Having reached Rantuka and having asked forgiveness again and again, one should then bathe in the Sarasvatī, behold the Yakṣa, and bow down to him. || 28 ||
Having offered flowers, incense, and food oblations, one should utter these words:
"O Lord of Yakṣas, by your grace, [may there be] forests and likewise rivers. (29)
"May no obstacle arise for me as I wander to the sacred fords; salutations!
Having thus propitiated the Lord of Yakṣas, one should properly undertake the pilgrimage. || 30 ||
O enchanting one, that man who makes a pilgrimage to Kurukṣetra, which bestows merit, as well as to forests, sacred fords, and rivers; || 31 ||
For him, there is no deficiency whatsoever in this world or in the next.

Thus ends the sixty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Dimensions and Other Characteristics of the Sacred Field," in the *Kuru-kṣetra-māhātmya* within the dialogue between Vasu and Mohini, in the *Bṛhad-upākhyāna* of the latter portion of the glorious *Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa*.
Now begins the sixty-fifth chapter.
Mohinī said:
"O best of Brahmins, what auspicious forests are there in that place?"
And tell me, in due order, of the river journeys that bestow all perfections.
Tell me of all those holy fords (*tīrtha*) that exist here in Kurukṣetra which bestow great merit, since you, O Guru, are the one who grants the ultimate goal.
Vasu said:
Listen, O Mohinī, I shall describe the merit-bestowing procedure for the pilgrimage to Kurukṣetra, by performing which one attains the supreme goal. || 3 ||
There are seven forests here in the midst of Kurukṣetra; I shall state their names for the sake of men who bestow merit in this world. || 4 ||
And the holy Kāmyaka forest, as well as the great Āditi-forest, the sacred forest of Vyāsa, and indeed the Phalakī-forest. || 5 ||
Likewise, Sūryavana and the meritorious Madhuvana are here, as well as the famous Sītāvana, which destroys the sins of men.
These seven forests are here, and within them are numerous sacred fords (tīrthas),
as well as the meritorious river Sarasvatī and the river Vaitaraṇī.
The Gaṅgā, the Mandākinī, and likewise other meritorious rivers— the Madhusravā,
the Dṛṣadvatī, the Kauśikī, and the meritorious river Hairaṇvatī.
Except for the Sarasvatī, the waters of these rivers are meritorious during the rainy season; they are pure for touching, drinking, and bathing.
Due to the power of this sacred field, these women do not experience menstruation;
however, having previously approached Rantuka, the gatekeeper of great strength— || 10 ||
Having paid homage to the Yakṣa, one should then commence the journey;
from there, O auspicious lady, a person should go to the great and meritorious Forest of Aditi.
Having bathed there, where Aditi performed great and perfect penance for the sake of a son, a woman should worship the Mother of the Gods.
She gives birth to a son who is a great hero, endowed with all auspicious marks;
from there, O lady of beautiful hips, one should go to the unsurpassed abode of Viṣṇu.
There is a famous place named Vimala where Hari is ever-present; having bathed in Vimala and beheld Vimaleśvara, a man [attains purity].
That Vimala attained the world of the Wheel-turning God of gods,
having seen Hari and Baladeva seated together upon a single throne.
One is instantly liberated from sin by this deluding [power]; of this there is no doubt.
Thereafter, one should go to the tīrtha known throughout the worlds as Pāriplava.
Having bathed there and drunk [the water], one who satisfies a Brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas with sacrificial fees and other gifts shall obtain the fruit of the Brāhma-sacrifice. || 17 ||
O auspicious lady, where there is the confluence of the Kauśikī which destroys sins, a man who bathes there with devotion attains union with his beloved.
Then, O highly fortunate lady, a man endowed with patience who reaches the Pṛthivītīrtha and bathes there with devotion attains the supreme goal. || 19 ||
Whatever offenses may have been committed by a person against the earth, the Goddess forgives them all for that embodied being who has bathed there.
Then, having beheld Śiva as Dakṣeśvara in the meritorious hermitage of Dakṣa, a human being obtains the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice. || 21 ||
Then one should go to Śālakinī; having bathed there, one should worship Hari together with Hara for the attainment of one's desired object. (22)
Then, having reached Nāgatīrtha and bathed there according to the prescribed rules, one who knows the ritual should consume ghee and curd, and shall indeed obtain freedom from fear of the nāgas.
Then, having returned in the evening, one who has stayed there for one night should worship the gatekeeper Rantuka on the following day.
Having honored a Brāhmaṇa with offerings of perfumes and other services,
one should then go to the Pañcanada tīrtha, renowned throughout the three worlds.
Because five roars, terrifying to the asuras, were uttered there by Hara,
it is named Pañcanada, which destroys all sins.
O Mohinī, from there one should go to Koṭitīrtha, where by bathing and giving gifts a man becomes fearless; it was there that Rudra [performed his penance].
Having brought ten million sacred sites (tīrthas), they were established there by that great-souled one;
having bathed in that tīrtha and beheld Hara as Koṭīśvara, a man [attains the fruit].
From that time forward, he shall always obtain the merit arising from the five great sacrifices;
and there itself, the Lord Vāmana was installed by all the gods.
Therefore, having worshipped him there, one obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice;
thereafter, having reached Aśvinī-tīrtha, one who is endowed with faith and has conquered the senses [attains further merit].
Having bathed there, a man shall become illustrious and handsome;
thereafter, he reaches the Vārāha-tīrtha, which was established by Viṣṇu.
Having bathed there with faith, a person shall attain a good state;
from there, O fair-faced one, he should go to Soma-tīrtha, where Soma resides.
Having performed austerities, he indeed became free from disease; one should perform a bath there and, by giving a single cow, obtain the fruit of a Rājasūya sacrifice. || 33 ||
Having worshipped Bhūteśvara, as well as Jvālāmāleśvara and the Tāṇḍaliṅga in that very place, one shall not undergo rebirth again. || 34 ||
Having bathed at Ekahaṃsa, a man obtains the fruit of giving a thousand cows;
having bathed at Kṛtaśauca, a man obtains the fruit of a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice. || 35 ||
Then, having reached the place named Muñjavaṭa belonging to the trident-bearing God,
and having stayed there for one night while worshipping the Lord, one becomes a leader of the Gaṇas.
Having propitiated the Yakṣiṇī stationed there at the gate, one who has observed a fast and bathed should honor and feed Brāhmaṇas for the pacification of great sins.
Having circumambulated it, one should then proceed to Puṣkara;
having bathed there and honored the ancestors, a man becomes one who has fulfilled his purpose. || 38 ||
And whoever performs the gift of a maiden there on the full moon day of Kārttika—
the deities, being well-pleased, shall grant him his desired fruit.
And the great yakṣa Kapila is stationed here as a gatekeeper;
he creates obstacles for the wicked and bestows the fruits of meritorious deeds. || 40 ||
His highly fortunate wife, named Ulūkhalamekhalā, would constantly beat a drum and wander about.
One should prevent sinners from bathing and likewise lead the doers of good deeds away;
then one should go to Rāmahrada and bathe there according to the prescribed ritual.
Having worshipped the gods, the ancestors, and the sages, one attains both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
by worshipping Rāma with true faith and giving gold, one becomes wealthy. (43)
Having reached Vaṃśamūla and bathed there, one shall uplift one's own lineage;
having bathed at Kāyaśodhanaka, with a purified body, one shall enter Hari.
Then, having attained the salvation of the world, and having bathed and worshipped Janārdana,
one reaches the eternal realm where the ancient Viṣṇu dwells.
Then, having reached the unsurpassed Śālagrāma at Śrītīrtha and having bathed there, he constantly worships Hari and beholds Him standing right before him.
Having reached the Kapilā-hrada, bathed there, and worshipped the gods and ancestors, one obtains the merit of a thousand tawny cows; of this there is no doubt.
O auspicious lady, by worshipping Kapila Viśveśa there according to the prescribed rites, one is honored by the gods and shall directly attain the state of Śiva.
Then, having fasted, one should worship the Sun at Sūryatīrtha;
having obtained the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, one shall go to heaven.
Gaṇapati himself stands at the entrance of the opening in the earth; having seen him and worshipped him there, one shall obtain the fruit of the sacrifice. || 50 ||
Having bathed in the Tīrtha of the Goddess, a man obtains supreme beauty;
having bathed in Brahmāvarta, a man attains the knowledge of Brahman. || 51 ||
Having bathed at Sutīrthaka and having duly honored the gods, sages, ancestors, and human beings, a man shall obtain the fruit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice. || 52 ||
Having bathed at the sacred ford of Kāmeśvara while endowed with faith, one is liberated from all diseases and attains the eternal Brahman. || 53 ||
O Goddess, for one who has bathed at Mātṛtīrtha and worships with faith, unsurpassed prosperity increases for seven generations of their lineage.
From there, one should go to Sītāvana; there is a great and auspicious tīrtha which, by its mere sight, purifies twenty-one generations of men.
By casting one's hair there, one indeed becomes purified of sin;
that sacred ford (tīrtha) there is renowned throughout the three worlds as Daśāśvamedhika.
By the mere sight of that sacred ford (tīrtha), one becomes liberated from sins; having then reached the sacred ford named Mānuṣa, one should perform an ablution.
O daughter of Vidhi, if one desires human birth again,
then at a distance of only one krośa from that human tīrtha, there is a great river.
There is a famous river named Apagā; having bathed there according to the prescribed rite, one should feed the best of the twice-born with śyāmāka grain cooked with milk. (59)
His sin goes to destruction, and the ancestors attain their proper state through the performance of śrāddha during the Mahālaya period in the dark fortnight of the month of Nabhasya.
On the fourteenth day, at midday, one who offers the funeral cakes (piṇḍa) shall attain liberation;
thereafter, one should go to Brāhmodumbaraka, the abode of Brahmā.
Having bathed there in the Brahmarsikuṇḍas, one obtains the fruit of the Soma sacrifice;
at the Vṛddhakedāraka Tīrtha, one beholds Sthāṇu accompanied by Daṇḍin.
Having worshipped there, a man obtains the power of invisibility at will;
from there he should go to Kalaśī, where the Goddess herself resides.
Having bathed in this [river] and worshipped Ambikā on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kṛṣṇa, one shall cross the ocean of saṃsāra after beholding the Lord Maheśvara.
A man endowed with faith attains the state of Śiva;
for there are thirty million sacred sites (tīrthas) present at Saraka, O beautiful lady.
Likewise, ten million Rudras are established in the well in the middle of that lake;
the man who bathes in that lake and remembers the ten million Rudras [attains great merit].
By that act, ten million Rudras would be worshipped; of this there is no doubt.
That very place is a site of endeavor, a sacred ford (tīrtha) that destroys all sins.
Having worshipped the gods and the hosts of ancestors residing there, where a human being attains liberation through mere sight alone— || 68 ||
One does not fall into an evil rebirth, but shall obtain whatever is desired by the mind;
and Kedāra is a great sacred ford that destroys all impurities. || 69 ||
Having bathed there, a person shall obtain the fruit of all gifts;
it is renowned as Anyajanma, situated to the east of Saraka. (70)
There is a great lake of clear water where the two gods Hari and Hara reside;
there Viṣṇu is four-armed, and Śiva stands in the form of a Liṅga. || 71 ||
Having bathed there and beheld them, a man who offers praise shall attain liberation;
then, having gone to the Nāga-hrada at the end of the bright fortnight of Caitra, he should bathe.
The performer of the śrāddha rite attains liberation and does not behold the world of Yama;
from there, one should go to Triviṣṭapa, a sacred ford frequented by the gods.
Having bathed there at the holy river Vaitaraṇī, which liberates one from sin, and having worshipped the trident-bearer whose banner is the bull; || 74 ||
With his soul purified of all sins, he indeed goes to the supreme goal;
having bathed in Rasāvarta, a man attains unsurpassed perfection.
Having bathed on the fourth lunar day of the bright fortnight of Caitra and having worshipped Śiva with devotion at Vilepaka, one is liberated from all sins.
From there, O Goddess, a man should go to the supreme Phalakinī forest,
where the gods together with the gandharvas perform supreme austerity.

Having bathed there in the river Dṛṣadvatī according to the prescribed rites and having offered libations to the gods and the ancestors, a man indeed partakes in the merit of the Agniṣṭoma and Atirātra sacrifices.
Likewise, whoever performs a śrāddha there on the day of the new moon (darśa) or the full moon (vidhu), obtains the supreme fruit equal to that of a śrāddha performed at Gayā. || 79 ||
In the Śrāddha rite, the remembrance of Araṇya bestows satisfaction upon the ancestors;
thereafter, at Pāṇighāta Tīrtha, a man should satiate the ancestors with libations.
Having obtained the fruit of the Rājasūya sacrifice and attained Sāṅkhya and Yoga, a mortal who then bathes according to the prescribed rule at the Miśraka Tīrtha [attains liberation].
Having obtained the fruit of all sacred fords (tīrthas), one attains the supreme goal; then, having gone to Vyāsa’s grove and bathed at the Manojava tīrtha, [one attains that same goal].
Having seen the all-pervading Manīṣin, a pure man obtains whatever he has meditated upon in his mind after going to Madhuvana and bathing in the Tīrtha of the Goddess.
Having bathed at the holy ford where the Kauśikī joins the Dṛṣadvatī, and having worshipped the gods and the seers, a man who has immersed himself there attains supreme perfection.
Restrained and restricted in diet, one is liberated from all sins;
from there, one should go to Vyāsasthaladya, where by the wise Vyāsa— || 85 ||
Overwhelmed by grief for his son, he had resolved to abandon his body;
however, having been raised up again by the gods who went there, he did not succumb to sorrow.
Having approached the Kinduśūka and offered a prastha of sesame seeds, one shall indeed attain supreme perfection; having died there, one shall obtain liberation. || 87 ||
Āhna and Mudita are two tirthas renowned on earth;
having bathed in those two, one whose soul is purified shall attain the world of the Sun.
Then, having gone to Mṛgamudya and standing there bowed before the Gaṅgā, one who worships Mahādeva shall obtain the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice. || 89 ||
Then, having gone to Koṭitīrtha and bathed there, one who views and praises Lord Śiva Koṭīśvara with faith shall obtain the fruit of ten million sacrifices.
From there, one should go to Vāmanaka, renowned throughout the three worlds,
where the birth of Vāmana occurred out of a desire to thwart the sacrifice of Bali.
Having bathed there at Viṣṇupada and having worshipped Vāmana, one whose self is purified of all sins is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu. || 92 ||
And right there is the Jyeṣṭhāśrama, which destroys all sins;
one should fast on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Jyeṣṭha and [bathe] on the following day.
Having bathed there according to the prescribed rite, one attains preeminence among men; O Goddess, a śrāddha performed there bestows supreme satisfaction upon the ancestors.
Right there is Koṭitīrtha, renowned throughout the three worlds;
having bathed in that sacred ford, a man shall obtain the fruit of ten million sacrifices.
There, having duly worshipped the god Maheśvara, known by the name Koṭīśvara, one shall attain the status of a Gaṇapati. || 96 ||
Having bathed at Sūryatīrtha in that very place, one becomes a partaker of the world of Ravi; then, having gone to the Kulottāraṇaka Tīrtha, one should perform a ritual bath.
Having uplifted his own lineage, he shall then dwell in heaven until the end of the kalpa,
after bathing in the lake of Pavana and beholding the god Maheśvara.
Liberated from all sins, he shall attain the state of Śiva;
by bathing in the Hanumat-tīrtha, a man shall obtain liberation.
Having bathed at the tīrtha of the royal sage Śālahotra, he was freed from sin; then, having bathed at the tīrtha of the Sarasvatī called Śrīkumbha, he became a speaker of sacrifice.
Having bathed in the Kuṇḍa at Naimiṣa, one partakes in the merit of bathing at Naimiṣa;
having bathed in the Vedavatī-tīrtha, a woman shall attain the state of a chaste wife (satī).
Having bathed at Brahmatīrtha, a man attains the status of a Brāhmaṇa;
he reaches the supreme abode of Brahmā, where having gone, one does not grieve.
Having bathed at Somatīrtha, a man shall attain the way to heaven;
and having reached Saptasārasvata Tīrtha and bathed there, he becomes a partaker of liberation.
There, the seven Sarasvatīs have come together in perfect unison: Suprabhā, Kāñcanākṣī, Viśālā, and Manoharī.
And Sunandā, Suveṇu, and the seventh, Vimalodakā—one who bathes likewise at the Ośanasa Tīrtha shall be liberated from sins. || 105 ||
Having bathed at Kapālamocana, even a slayer of a Brahmin is indeed purified;
a man who has bathed at Vaiśvāmitra shall attain the status of a Brāhmaṇa.
Then, having bathed at Pṛthūdaka, one is released from the bondage of worldly existence;
having bathed at Avakīrṇa, a man obtains the fruit of celibacy.
Then, having gone to Madhusrāva and bathed, one is liberated from sins;
and by bathing at the Vāsiṣṭha tīrtha, one attains the world of Vasiṣṭha. || 108 ||
Having bathed at the confluence of the Aruṇā and fasted for three nights, a man attains liberation after bathing; there is no need for further deliberation on this matter. || 109 ||
There are four oceans there; a man who bathes in them obtains the merit of giving a thousand cows and is glorified in the heavenly world. || 110 ||

And there is another sacred ford there called Somatīrtha; having bathed in it on the sixth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, O Mohinī, and having performed a Śrāddha, one shall deliver one's ancestors.
Then, having bathed at Pañcavaṭa and having worshipped Śiva, who bears the form of Yoga, according to the prescribed rite, he rejoices together with the deities.
Then, having bathed at Kurutīrtha, one shall obtain all perfections;
a mortal who has plunged into Svargadvāra is glorified in the heavenly world.
Having bathed at that non-hellish sacred ford, one is liberated from all sins;
from there, O Goddess, a man should go to the excellent Kāmyaka forest.
Upon merely entering it, one is liberated from all accumulations;
then, having reached Ādityavana, one becomes a partaker of liberation simply through the sight of it. 115.
Having performed a bath there on a Sunday, one shall obtain one's desire;
having bathed at Yajñopavītīka, one becomes a partaker of the fruits of one's own dharma. || 116 ||
Then, having bathed in the holy ford known as Catuḥpravāha, that best of men obtains the fruit of all sacred fords and rejoices in heaven like a god. || 117 ||
Having bathed at a sacred ford (tīrtha) within a monastery (vihāra), one shall obtain all happiness;
having bathed at a difficult-to-access ford, a man shall not fall into a miserable state.
Then, having bathed in the Sarasvatī-kūpa, also known as Pitṛ-tīrtha, and having offered libations to the gods and others, one attains the supreme goal. || 119 ||
Having bathed in the Prācīsarasvatī and performed the Śrāddha ceremony according to the prescribed rules,
one shall obtain even that which is difficult to attain, and at the end of the body, one shall attain the heavenly realm.
Having bathed at Śukratīrtha, a man who performs a śrāddha ceremony— especially on the eighth or fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Caitra— shall deliver his ancestors.
Fasting at Brahmatīrtha, one becomes a partaker of liberation; of this there is no doubt.
Then, having bathed at Sthāṇutīrtha and beheld Sthāṇuvaṭa, a man [attains the same]. (122)
"One is liberated from terrible sins," so said the Grandfather (Brahmā);
by the mere sight of the Sthāṇu-liṅga, the pilgrimage becomes complete. || 123 ||
O Goddess of the Gods, I have spoken the truth, the absolute truth: there has never been, nor will there ever be, a sacred site equal to Kurukṣetra. (124)
Having performed the twelve pilgrimages there, one is no longer subject to rebirth;
[one has thereby] fulfilled the rites of public works (pūrta), sacrifice (iṣṭa), austerity (tapas), oblation (huta), and charity (datta) according to the prescribed rules.

In that regard, those learned in the Vedas know that everything becomes inexhaustible on the occasion of Manu and the other world-protectors, at the beginning of the Yugas, and during the eclipses of the moon and the sun. (126)
Whether one has entered upon a great calamity or on an auspicious day, by bathing there at Kurukṣetra, one obtains infinite fruit. || 127 ||
For the purification of the sinful born in the Kali age, the high-souled Brahmā ordained Kurukṣetra as a bliss-bestowing sacred field.
The man who, with devotion, recites or hears this meritorious narrative that destroys sin, is also liberated from all sins. || 129 ||
Whatever one gives there at Kurukṣetra during a solar eclipse,
that very thing a person obtains perpetually in birth after birth.
Now, what is the use of much speaking? O knower of the rules, listen to this certainty: one who desires liberation from worldly existence should indeed resort to Kurukṣetra. (131)
This alone is great merit, this alone is the greatest [merit], and this alone is great knowledge: that one should go to Sthāṇutīrtha. || 132 ||
There is no other auspicious sacred site on earth equal to Kurukṣetra, where one may attain liberation whether one is of good conduct or lacks good conduct. (133)
O sinless one, all this that you asked me has been narrated— the majesty of Kurukṣetra, which destroys all sins.
It bestows merit and liberation as well; what else do you wish to hear? || 135 ||

Thus ends the sixty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Pilgrimage," in the *Kurukṣetra-māhātmya*, within the dialogue between Vasu and Mohinī, in the latter part of the *Bṛhad-upākhyāna* of the glorious *Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa*. || 65 ||
Thus ends the *Mahātmya* of Kurukṣetra. Now begins the *Mahātmya* of Gaṅgādvāra.
This is the sixty-sixth chapter.
Mohinī said: O best among the foremost of the twice-born, I have heard from you the great majesty of Kurukṣetra, which removes sins and bestows all perfections upon men. (1)
O Guru, may you be blessed; please describe that sacred ford known as Gaṅgādvāra which brings merit, for my heart desires to hear it. || 2 ||
Vasu said:
Listen, O blessed lady, I shall proclaim the merit-bestowing greatness of Gaṅgādvāra, which destroys sin and brings auspiciousness to those who hear it or recite it. || 3 ||
There, the glorious Gaṅgā, known as Alakanandā, having reached the earth and followed the chariot of Bhagīratha, pierced the mountains by the thousands.
That field where Dakṣa Prajāpati formerly sacrificed to the Lord of Sacrifice bestows merit upon men and destroys all their sins.
In that sacrifice, the gods, led by Indra, being duly summoned,
arrived together with their respective hosts, desiring to receive their sacrificial portions.
Where the celestial sages and the stainless Brahman-sages have arrived, together with their disciples and grand-disciples, as well as the royal sages, O auspicious one.
All the Gandharvas, Apsarases, Yakṣas, Siddhas, Vidyādharas, and Uragas were invited by that wise son of Brahmā. || 8 ||
They reached the sacrificial ground, with the exception of Śarva, the wielder of the Pināka bow;
then, as those travelers in celestial chariots proceeded together with their beloveds, [the following occurred].
Hearing the descriptions of the festival of Dakṣa’s sacrifice being joyfully recounted to one another, the beautiful Satī became filled with longing and entreated Mahādeva.
Having heard that, the Blessed One said, "It is not better to go there," yet he disregarded the god out of respect for the inevitability of what was to happen.
O blessed lady, she went alone to see the festival of her father's sacrifice;
having arrived there, she was not welcomed by anyone.
The slender-limbed woman gave up her life-breaths; that place became an excellent sacred field (kṣetra).
Those who bathe in that holy ford (tīrtha) and offer libations to the gods and the ancestors [attain great merit].
They shall be most beloved of the Goddess and partakers solely in worldly enjoyment and liberation—those others as well who there renounce their own lives through fasting and other such means. (14)
Having attained Śiva directly, they do not undergo birth again;
then, having heard that from Nārada, the Lord Nīlalohita [spoke].
Upon hearing of the death of his beloved wife, he created Vīrabhadra;
accompanied by all the Pramathas, he utterly destroyed that sacrifice.
Furthermore, being immediately propitiated by the request of Vidhi, the Bountiful One (Śiva) performed the sacrifice again, restoring the modified rite to its original state. || 17 ||
Then that incomparable tirtha, which destroys all sins,
came into being, where Soma, having bathed, was liberated from the affliction of consumption.

In that place, whoever bathes according to the prescribed rite and contemplates whatever desire they may have, attains each and every one of them; for one who knows the ritual, there should be no doubt in this matter. (19)
Where the imperishable Lord Viṣṇu, the Lord of Sacrifice himself,
was praised by Dakṣa and the gods— that sacred ford is named Hari.

In that regard, whatever mortal bathes according to the prescribed rule when the feet of Hari are present shall become beloved of Viṣṇu and the sole recipient of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. || 21 ||
Therefore, in the eastern direction, there is a famous sacred field named Trigaṅga, where the triple-pathed river is visibly seen by all people.
Having bathed there and then offered libations to the gods, sages, ancestors, and men, a mortal endowed with perfect faith rejoices in heaven like a god.
In that regard, whoever gives up their life when the current has set in shall go to the abode of Viṣṇu, being duly honored by the gods. || 24 ||
Then, having fasted for three nights and bathed at the Kanakhala tirtha situated in the southern direction, one is liberated from all sins.
Furthermore, O Goddess, he who should give a cow there to a Brahmin who has mastered the Vedas shall never behold the Vaitaraṇī river or Yama.
Whatever is chanted, offered in sacrifice, practiced as austerity, or given here attains infinity;
so too at this very Jahnu-tīrtha, where in ancient times by Jahnu— || 27 ||
That river was drunk up by the royal sage after he had taken it into his mouth as a mouthful; being appeased, it was released by him and emerged from his ear.
O highly fortunate lady, having bathed there, the man who, endowed with faith and observing a fast, should worship a Brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas; || 29 ||
He who feeds [the deity] with supreme food shall dwell in heaven for a kalpa;
thereafter, O slender-waisted one, one should go to Koṭitīrtha situated in the western direction.
Whereby ten millionfold merit would arise from seeing a lord of ten million,
by staying there for a single night one would obtain the merit of [seeing] Puṇḍarīka.
Likewise, O Goddess, in the northern direction there is a supreme sacred site (tīrtha) renowned as Saptagaṅgā, which destroys all sins.
O high-minded one, having bathed separately in all those holy hermitages of the Seven Sages and having offered libations to the deities; || 33 ||
A mortal obtains the ancestors and the eternal world of the sages when the celestial river was brought down by King Bhagīratha.
Then, for their pleasure, she became sevenfold-streamed; consequently, that sacred ford (tīrtha) attained renown on earth as Saptagaṅga. || 35 ||
Having reached Āvarta thereafter and having gratified the ancestors headed by the gods, he bathes and rejoices in the abode of the Lord of the Gods for an entire Yuga.
Then, O blessed lady, having reached the supreme Kapilā-hrada and having given a cow to an eminent brahmin, one obtains the fruit of giving a thousand cows. || 37 ||
Right here is the supremely purifying sacred ford of the Naga King; whoever performs an ablution here shall obtain fearlessness from serpents.
Then, having reached Lalitaka, the supreme tirtha of Śantanu,
and having bathed and offered libations according to the rules to the gods and others, one attains the highest goal.
In that very place where Gaṅgā, having been obtained by Śantanu, had assumed human form, she abandoned her body after giving birth to the Vasus year after year.
His body fell there, and there he took birth as a bear; the man who bathes there and eats that medicinal herb [is purified]. (41)
By the grace of Gaṅgādevī, that virtuous man who reaches Bhīmasthala and bathes there does not fall into an evil rebirth. || 42 ||
Having enjoyed pleasures here in this world, one shall attain the state of heaven at the end of the body;
these holy places, O Goddess, have been described to you in brief.
O highly fortunate lady, there are indeed thousands of other [tirthas] there;
yet, whatever man should bathe in this field when the sun is in Aquarius, in Jupiter, and in Virgo, [attains the supreme goal].
He was indeed a master of speech in person, like another Sun-god;
then, when he had traveled to the holy pilgrimage sites such as Prayāga and Pṛthūka.
Now, whoever should bathe according to the prescribed rule during the Vāruṇa yoga, as well as the Mahāvāruṇaka and the Mahāmahāvāruṇa [yogas], [attains the fruit]. || 46 ||
By worshipping the Brāhmaṇas with devotion on the occasion of a Saṅkrānti, or on the new moon day, or during the Vyatīpāta yoga, or at the beginning of a Yuga, he shall attain the state of Brahman.
Furthermore, whatever gift one may offer on an auspicious day to any ascetic, that shall become ten millionfold; this which I have spoken is the truth. (48)
Whatever man, even while staying at a great distance, should remember Gaṅgādvāra,
he attains a good state, just as one who remembers Hari at the time of death.
O Goddess, whatever deity a self-restrained man worships at Haridvāra, that very deity, being well-pleased, shall fulfill his heart's desires. (50)
This alone is the place for austerity, this alone is the place for recitation,
and this alone is the place for oblation, where the Gaṅgā has reached the earth.
That mortal who, having bathed there, recites the thousand names of Gaṅgā at the three times of day, shall obtain imperishable progeny. || 52 ||
O highly fortunate lady, whoever listens to this Purāṇa with devotion and according to the prescribed rules at Gaṅgādvāra goes to the imperishable state.
That best of men who hears the majesty of Haridvāra, or reads it endowed with devotion, shall also obtain the fruit of bathing there.
O Goddess, in whichever house this greatness is written, there shall be no fear of snakes, thieves, fire, malevolent planets, or kings. 55.
All prosperities increase through the grace of Lord Viṣṇu. || 56 ||

Thus ends the sixty-sixth chapter, titled "The Greatness of Haridvāra," in the dialogue between Vasu and Mohinī, within the Bṛhad-upākhyāna of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa, in its latter section. || 66 ||
Thus ends the majesty of Gaṅgādvāra and Haridvāra. Now begins the majesty of Badarī.
This is the sixty-seventh chapter.
Mohinī said:
"O best of the twice-born, you have now described the greatness arising from Gaṅgādvāra; tell me now of the sin-destroying majesty of Badarī."
Vasu said:
Listen, O blessed lady, I shall proclaim the greatness arising from Badarī, hearing which a living being is liberated from the bondage of birth and saṃsāra. || 2 ||
The sacred field of Hari known as Badarī destroys all sins, grants liberation to those afraid of worldly existence, and removes the defects of the Kali age for men. || 3 ||
Where the divine Nārāyaṇa and the blessed Ṛṣi Nara, having taken birth from Dharma in bodily form, went to Gandhamādana.
O highly fortunate one, we two shall remain at that place where the Badarī tree stands, endowed with many fragrant fruits, performing penance until the end of the kalpa.
Surrounded by the best of sages such as Nārada and others, as well as by hosts of Siddhas residing in Kalāpagrāma, they remained established for the stability of the worlds.
There exists the famous Agnitīrtha, which bestows all spiritual perfections;
having bathed there, even those who have committed great sins are purified of their transgressions.
Just as base gold is purified when smelted in fire,
so too a person, by bathing in the Agnitīrtha, is liberated from sins.
Whatever fruit a mortal obtains through thousands of Cāndrāyaṇa fasts and even through ten million Kṛcchra penances, that is obtained by bathing at Vahnitīrtha.
O daughter of Brahmā, there are five rocks at that holy site; situated in their midst is Agnitīrtha, which destroys sins merely by being seen.
There, the venerable Nārada performed most severe penance;
that stone is named Nāradī, which grants liberation merely by being seen.
O fair-eyed one, where the presence of Hari is ever-present,
there is the Nārada-kuṇḍa, wherein a man who bathes becomes pure.

Whatever one may desire—whether worldly enjoyment, liberation, or devotion to Hari—one shall obtain it by performing with devotion bathing, giving gifts, and worshiping the gods in this [tīrtha]. (13)
Whatever one performs there—be it a fire sacrifice, recitation, or anything else—that becomes inexhaustible;
furthermore, another stone of Vainateya in that sacred field brings auspiciousness.
There, the high-souled Garuḍa performed intense austerities for thirty thousand years with the desire to behold Hari.
Then, O auspicious lady, the Blessed One, being pleased, granted him a boon:
"May you be invincible to the hosts of Daityas and terrifying even to the Nāgas. (16)
